They tell the story of a crew looking to escape from the company using a ship on Repress and flying to a moon in a different region known as 495-Risk. One of the crew members died to a Masked on Rend. The fate of the remaining crew is unknown.

Text ⁠
-9th of July 2349-
I found a couple floppy discs in a cabinet somewhere in the building.
Allows me to put down my thoughts using the big computer in the hangar.

First I'll introduce myself, hi, I'm Dan. It's been 7 days since I started working for the company.
Lucky for me I was greeted by a set of kind faces. They sort of explained to me how things work around here.
We're a crew of 4, there's Berry, he's pretty funny and good at keeping our spirits up. Then there's Kate who has been here the longest, used to be a mechanic for a failed business.
And there's Arnold. Big guy, pretty smart as well, we call him engine man cause he's always the one carrying the engines hehe.
(I'm also fairly certain Kate and Arnold have a thing for each other)
Don't tell them I wrote that, they'll kill me

It's been rough. We've been going from building to building day by day delivering all our Junk to the company building.
Can't say I'm quite fond of the place. The company desk reeks, it's nasty. And not only that but the building itself is quite imposing.
I don't understand why but it feels like it wants to crush me like I'm an ant in the kitchen.

Same with this place, though I feel a bit more safe here, its less menacing. Less like I'm being watched constantly.
I'm not the only one who feels that way.
Arnold hates the company building too. He's always said there's something off about it.
Maybe he's on to something.

Either way Kate just radioed in that it's getting late. I better get going.
I'll write more when I can.

Text ⁠
-12th of July 2349-
Okay where do I start. First of all. There have been several near death experiences.
The quota is starting to get dangerously high. And Berry has seemingly cought the flu.

It's been rough.

Last thing we expected was to enter an insane asylum back on Vow. I don't think I ever want to go back there.
Berry stayed for ship duty this time due him getting sick. So me, Kate and Arnold went in. The place looked haunted.
It might as well have been because I swear I saw a trash can move. Arnold also claims to have seen a dark figure briefly staring at him when he opened a door before it vanished.
Terrifying.
That wasn't the strangest part though. We heart Kate scream a few hallways down.. and when we got there, Blood was still freshly dripping from the ceiling. Guts, pieces of skin and hair littered the floor.
We were horrified. We thought it was maybe a mine or.. something worse. Either way we were in shock.
Too scared to continue we retreated back to the entrance. But when we got there, there she was completely fine carrying a hairdryer and rubik's cube.
Arnold immediately ran over. Which I guess confirms my little theory heh.
Nevertheless it was unusual to say the least. I'm going to have nightmares about that for a while.

But then I knew one thing for certain. I want to leave.
They felt the same way.
The ship would only route to a few company issued moons. None are really suitable for hiding out.
Arnold suggested to mess with the terminal to see if we could get it to route us somewhere else.
When Kate inspected it though she said doing that would trigger some form of protocol which would send us flying into space...
I fear then we might have discovered what happens if we don't make quota.
If true the company is much worse than we initially thought.

However Berry actually made a pretty good remark, he asked if we could take one of the ships back on Repress.
We had enough credits to go there soo.. now were here.
None of the ships were really usuable except for this one older model.
Kate said she can patch it up given enough time, it's missing a few components but we might be able to get those during the next quota.
There is hope.

Text ⁠
-16th of July 2349-
I have unfortunate news.
Yesterday we lost Berry..

We went to Rend and everyone headed out to look for bolts, screws, metal plating, toy robots for wiring we could use on the new ship.
Of course we left Berry in the ship, he was still sick but starting to recover.
He was great at communicating during ship duty, even though he felt like shit he was still able to crack a few jokes over the walkie.
I remember him asking *What's the best animal to bring to the battlefield... DUCK!!* its so stupid its funny.
We knew something was up when it went silent though.
And sure enough when we headed back I faintly saw him roam around in the snow covered in red goop wearing a comedy mask, like he was possessed.
None of us had the strength to put him down if he was still in there so we just.. left.
I'll miss him.

Kate and Arnold are now properly together, happy for them. They fit each other well.
Stress is starting to take me though.. I feel a constant pressure as we're racing against the clock.
Makes me feel dizzy at times.

The ship is almost ready luckily. Good thing because our quota is reaching scarily high.
Especially with Berry gone we're not even sure if we'll make it past the next one.
We just need a control panel. None of us have seen one just yet but tomorrow we're making a visit to Titan, hopefully we'll find one there.
We have already planned out a place to escape to.
There's this city on a moon far from this region. 495-Risk. Fitting name I suppose.
Once we get there we'll be safe. Hopefully.
I'll write again when we return for hopefully our final visit.

• The "insane asylum" on Vow mentioned in Insanity is the Rubber Rooms interior, which has a 16.44% chance to spawn on Vow by default.
  • Out from all Wesley's Moons, Repress has the highest interior size multiplier.

Crew: ?

CONDITION: Intact, aged, few components destroyed.

Contains several hazardous substances and Fauna.

The player's clock is hidden while on ResearcherxB. However, time progresses at its normal speed. ResearcherxB's exterior will also have its lights turned off if the power in the interior is turned off.

In the main corridor to the left after exiting the ship, there are several doors the player can open or shut from that side. At the end of this corridor is a door that requires a keycard to open, which "Cavil's keycard" is a guaranteed scrap spawn within the interior. Opening this door leads to a room covered in white mold, and similarly has the mold spikes found on the exterior of Vindict. Five random scrap from ResearcherxB's Loot Table is guaranteed to spawn on a table in this room. Two terminals can also be interacted with in this room and the one next to the left ship lever will unlock Carnate.

Additionally, a panel immediately to the right can be moved to reveal eight differently colored wires and two valves. Players must cut the colored wires that have a red light above them at one or two panels. One is on the wall in the big room to the left of the main corridor and the other is on the wall next to a regular door to the left of the main entrance. Cutting a wrong wire will deal 100 damage to the player. Afterwards, players must return to the original panel and repeatedly interact with the valves.

Finally, players can decide to overload ResearcherxB by interacting with the left ship lever in this room after completing the above puzzle. If pulled, players will receive a warning that the ship will explode in 30 seconds. The autopilot will leave after these 30 seconds and all players still on the exterior or in the interior will be abandoned. Players can still route to ResearcherxB afterward, but there will be nothing there other than the debris floating in space. This change is permanent on that save file, will prevent ResearcherxB from crash landing onto and infecting Trite, and cause debris from ResearcherxB to fall randomly onto the exteriors of some moons.

Setting up a Triangulation Device on Vindict and another six random moons as prompted. This must be accomplished within a random number of days of in-game time, as ResearcherxB can no longer be located and will begin to crash onto Trite otherwise. This change is permanent on that save file. Players can receive at least three distress signals from the ship while on a moon and each signal warns players of how many days are remaining. Being fired will reset triangulation progress but will not affect the countdown.

Triangulation Devices can be crafted on Galetry or Gratar. Additionally, there is a chance to find a device on the exteriors of Glace, Selector, Trite, and Vindict on caches of scrap that can be collected once per save file. Excluding the "Recovery order", this scrap is randomized per landing and players can reroll what scrap is there by not getting too close to the cache.

Carnate: Interact with the terminal past the keycard door and to the left of the ship lever. If ResearcherxB crashes or is blown up before interacting with the terminal, Carnate will be inaccessible on that save file.

Text ⁠
Transcript security recording - Day 16
—----------------------- 10:36 - Lab

S. Dent: I think that’s it. I think we’ve got it. This will be perfect when it’s merged with the main compound.
C. Darter: Yeah.. that’s great.
S. Dent: Is something wrong? I thought you’d be celebrating.
C. Darter: I don’t think we’re doing the right thing.
S. Dent: How so? We’re helping people. If not for the Triton Empire we’re saving people’s lives with this.
S. Dent: Are we not? Cavil?
C. Darter: They uh.. You aren’t allowed to know but it’s likely not for the purpose you’ve been led to believe.
S. Dent: What do you mean? This is medicine, it will protect people.
C. Darter: Yes but. Not the people you might think.
S. Dent: Well.. Go on.
C. Darter: This is part of Project Mycete. A project where they’re attempting to make enhanced soldiers by stuffing them with experimental drugs.
S. Dent: What.
C. Darter: And.. not only that but out there people are being slaughtered, tortured and murdered in pursuit of people fit for the procedure.
S. Dent: WHAT.
S. Dent: All this time. I have been working for a lie. Harming these poor creatures. Just so we have a small step up in this conquest??.
C. Darter: .. Basically.
S. Dent: Why didn’t you tell me?
C. Darter: I mean, they will likely have me repurposed when they discover I have now leaked this information.. It’s more of an execution than a repurpose.
S. Dent: Right. So. What now?. Do we leave? Do we burn it all? Tell me.
C. Darter: I need time to think. I don’t want to hand Sol this research. We’ll talk about this tomorrow. Pretend like none of this happened.
S. Dent: Yeah. Okay. Simple. I’ll just simply pretend like I haven’t spent the past two and half weeks risking my life for a lie.
C. Darter: I mean it.
—----------------------- 16:13 - Office

J. Charter: Sarah? Are you okay?
S. Dent: I’m fine.
J. Charter: The tears running down your face say otherwise. Did something happen?
S. Dent: I would prefer not to talk about it.
J. Charter: Something personal?
S. Dent: Yea.
J. Charter: I see.. If something is up you can talk to me about it, it’s okay.
S. Dent: Wouldn’t want it to be a detriment to the mission would you.
J. Charter: What?
S. Dent: No I mean. I’m sorry. I don’t know where that came from. It’s just hard. I’m not sure if I can take much more of it.
J. Charter: It’s okay, I get it.
S. Dent: Did Cavil send you?
J. Charter: No he didn’t.
S. Dent: What made you come here?
J. Charter: Well you’ve seemed a bit down today. It’s important that everyone on this crew feels okay. And I also care.. about.. you. I mean..
S. Dent: Thank you, I really appreciate it. There’s just.. Maybe I miss home and it’s wearing me down.
J. Charter: That makes sense. I can’t say I don’t miss it back there. Sooner or later we’ll be back. We just have to complete our mission. We’ll be okay.
S. Dent: Yeah. Thank you, really.

Text ⁠
Transcript security recording - Day 17 
—----------------------- 18:56 - Maintenance tunnel

C. Darter: Hopefully nobody can hear us down here.
S. Dent: Hope so too. Have you got an idea?
C. Darter: I have a plan. It will be hairy.
S. Dent: Alright. Can’t be worse than whatever they’re doing out there.
C. Darter: It’s a two part plan. We have to destroy the autopilot. And manually route it somewhere else so they won’t be able to find it. I wrote the coordinates on this note. Send this ship here.
S. Dent: Uhm. Okay. What will you do?
C. Darter: I’ll make sure they won’t be able to track the ship anymore and prepare the escape pod.
S. Dent: What about Julian? We tell him right?
C. Darter: It’s better if we don’t. He’s loyal to the Triton Empire. I don’t trust him to betray that.
S. Dent: Well we can’t just leave him. Maybe he’ll listen to me.
C. Darter: It’d be best not to try. He might sound the alarm.
S. Dent: I won’t leave him.
C. Darter: If you can convince him to join us in the escape pod he can come with. But only after you’ve done your part.
S. Dent: Right, If this is another lie I’ll kill you.
C. Darter: I promise.
S. Dent: When do we start?
C. Darter: 22:00. I’ll have the escape pod ready by 23:30. Be there.
S. Dent: Okay.
C. Darter: I have some digging to do. Good luck.
S. Dent: You too.

—----------------------- 22:24 - Security office

J. Charter: The fuck.

—----------------------- 22:38 - Cockpit

J. Charter: Who’s there? Sarah?
S. Dent: Julian?
J. Charter: What are you doing? Did you mess with the autopilot?
S. Dent: I can explain.
J. Charter: Is this an order? Why are you doing this?
S. Dent: This is not right.
J. Charter: What do you mean?.
S. Dent: This whole project is wrong. We’re not helping anyone with this. It won’t be for medicine. We’re developing weapons.
J. Charter: I know. This is a military operation, as was stated in my briefing.
S. Dent: You knew? This whole time? They’re torturing people. Just so they can experiment on the survivors with this. You’re okay with that?
J. Charter: People suffer either way. Whether we complete this mission or not. You know that. We could be part of something great.
S. Dent: If we are building a future like this.. I want none of it.
J. Charter: You’re a traitor.
S. Dent: Please, think about it. We can escape this. Leave it behind. Knowing we won’t have innocent blood on our hands.
J. Charter: I trusted you, Cavil trusted you. Why would you sabotage the mission. We were going home. We were..
S. Dent: Cavil is preparing the escape pod. Please just come with me.
J. Charter: You all Lied to me. You betrayed me.
S. Dent: Please Julian, they are evil.
J. Charter: Why.
S. Dent: Julian, please. Calm down, Lower your weapon and join me. We’ll be okay.
S. Dent: Please calm down, Julian, please. Juli-.
J. Charter: I.. I’m sorry.

—----------------------- 23:13 - Central hallway

J. Charter: I’m sorry Sarah. I love you.

—----------------------- 23:16 - Cargo bay

J. Charter: I’m sorry.

Text ⁠
Transcript security recording - Day 18
—----------------------- 00:23 - Pod-1

C. Darter: These might be the last words you’ll hear from me. Escape pods don’t have a great track record when it comes to landings.
C. Darter: Sarah is dead. The damn bastard shot her in the neck. Following orders before he launched himself out the airlock. Watched him sobbing through the hallway.
C. Darter: I didn’t want them to get hurt. It just happened.
C. Darter: She was innocent.
C. Darter: Sol, if you ever read the logs. I want you to know I’m not sorry for sabotaging your mission. You are a corrupt piece of shit who deserves to be put with the innocents you’re slaughtering.
C. Darter: I’ve got your documents. I’ve read your history. You were always like this.
C. Darter: Watch what happens when the common people figure out who you really are.

POPULATION: Moved

CONDITIONS: Dark, warm, moist, rich in diverse flora

FAUNA: Dominated by Baboon Hawks and Elders.

Unfinished Section

This section seems unfinished. If you're a wiki editor, please help with completing this section.
Roart can experience Flooded, Eclipsed, or Earthquakes weather by default.
On Roart you can hear two ambiences. One plays inside while the other one plays outside.
The Elder is an entity that can exclusively spawn on the exterior of Roart during the day. It is a variant of the Forest Keeper that is larger, louder, has a max count of 1, and has 80hp.

Roart's exterior has several small and large purple roses that temporarily trap any player that walks into them. The smaller roses deal 22 damage and the larger roses deal 90 damage to the player before releasing them. Several small roses also spawn in the interior.

Roart features a trial that generates on the exterior. Completing it rewards the player with scrap worth ▮600-1000. The specific reward is a "Soul orb".

To complete this trial:

  1. Acquire four "Human heart" scrap. There is a very low chance for it to spawn within the interior, so the easiest ways to get multiple are through the gift shop on Galetry or through the hidden chamber on the exterior of Thalasso. This scrap is not to be confused with the vanilla "Heart" scrap that can randomly spawn within the interior of Dine in v73.
  2. From the back of and facing toward the ship, turn right, turn left, turn far right, turn left onto the path with purple roses, and continue straight until reaching the green lights with multiple altars.
  3. Drop the hearts into the altars of blood as prompted.
  4. Jump into the blue light to be teleported to an altered version of the exterior. Jumping back into the blue light teleports back to the regular exterior.
  5. Turn right out of the altar area and follow the lights until reaching a stone platform.
  6. Find Emma, who typically spawns in the nearby area, interact with her to retrieve her body, and place the body onto the top of the platform.
  7. Emma will begin screaming and cause the entire area except for the stone platform to be covered in a thick fog that deals 1 damage per hit to any player inside. Interact with the blade.
  8. Emma will begin to retaliate by summoning apparitions that deal 49 damage to the player on contact. Interact with the blade again.
  9. Emma's apparitions will appear and move faster. Interact with the blade again.
  10. After successfully chopping off Emma's head, grab it and go to the map at the bottom of the stone platform to find the location to bury it. This location is marked by the shovel and an X, the map location is marked by the star, and the teleporter back to the regular exterior is circled with arrows pointing to it.
  11. Interact with the mound surrounded by candles to bury Emma's head.
  12. After a short time, all players will be teleported back to regular exterior and the "Soul orb" scrap will spawn on the now closed off teleporter.

    On average, beating this trial requires around ▮328 or more depending on how the hearts are acquired and rewards the player with around ▮800. It is possible to reach the altered exterior with a jetpack, but this is pointless because the four hearts must be dropped into the altar for the reward to spawn regardless of when the head is buried.

We are the hands that bury the deceased, you are the shovel that keep the hands from getting stained. We cannot allow the deceased to control who lives and who dies. Find the forsaken child, dispose of her body and we will let you out.
• Before "Obscurity" video material on "Bury the child" videotape was different:

The main entrance of the Rubber Rooms interior.

The Rubber Rooms are a psych ward themed interior. It most commonly spawns on Xenphir and has a rare chance to spawn on any moon.

• Reception - The main entrance always generates with a receptionist desk in front of it.
  • Coffin - A coffin in a room typically found near the main entrance. This coffin has the reward for completing a Secondary Objective.
  • Cells - Various small rooms with an assortment of furniture and other items in them.
  • Padded Cells - More confined cells that can connect to the titular Rubber Rooms.
  • Rubber Rooms - Accessed by walking through the fog in some Padded Cells, teleporting players to an area directly above the interior with padded white walls. Scrap can spawn here and entities can enter and leave this area.
  • Morgues - Rooms with several trays for bodies. Players can interact with some of the doors to open a tray and potentially reveal scrap. One of the morgues will only generate trays for the Discover the Body objective.
  • Offices - Larger rooms with large tables, many chairs, etc. Scrap can spawn in them.
  • Library - A section of the interior with several bookshelves. Scrap can spawn here.
  • Cafeteria - A large cafeteria room with a kitchen.
  • Operating Room - A room down a narrow staircase often with the corpse of an employee. Frequently has scrap inside it.
  • Nursery - A room for children with small cradles. A baby is often heard crying until players approach the cradle the sound is coming from. Scrap can spawn here.
  • Haunted Apparatus - A door will open by itself to a long hallway that leads to a room with a door, an electric chair, and a white apparatus. It is worth ▮90, is two-handed, and weighs 8lbs. Taking the apparatus will cause the door to briefly shut and cause blood to come out of the chair. The door will then open back up to a now shifting hallway with the blood surging down it. Players must run back through this hallway without the blood catching up to them or they will die, which is possible if the player weighs 8lbs and begins sprinting the moment the door opens. The door at the end will swing open on its own again before shutting behind the player.

• Spooks - Various spooks and scares can occur in the interior, such as an eyeball appearing through the window of a door, lights exploding, book cases falling, etc. These spooks can be disabled in the Magic Wesley Rubber Rooms config.
  • Rats - Sometimes rats can be found skittering around. There are small holes in the wall that they can crawl out of. These are harmless. Rarely, a much larger rat with glowing red eyes can run through the walls with a loud sound effect accompanying it. This is also harmless.
  • Shifting Hallway - A hallway that moves up or down a level after being walked through. This always generates next to the main entrance room. Can be disorienting when trying to navigate.
  • Infinite Hallway - A hallway where the end is shrouded in a dark fog, and passing through the fog transports the player to a hallway that loops so long as they keep walking ahead. Turning around and going back is a good way to get out. The hallway has two different exit points.
  • Eclipsed - When this interior is on a moon that is Eclipsed, bloodstains will be everywhere. Additionally, the Haunted Apparatus hallway will shift more and slightly reduce visibility with a grainy-like effect when pulled.

• Spooky Door - A red door with an X on it can sometimes be immediately opened and will remain open for the rest of the day. However, if a player opens this door from a specific direction an infinite, mirror-like hallway will apear with a floating head rapidly approaching the player. It will deal 666 damage to the player if not closed in time. The door will take half a second to close with the prompt being replaced with the text "SHUT THE DOOR" and will open itself back up after successfully shutting it. This door can be disabled in the Magic Wesley Rubber Rooms config.
  • Fake Fire Exit - A fire exit door that always spawns on a tile with a black and white floor and red walls. Additionally, the hand symbol that appears for interacting with this door is noticeably bigger than an ordinary door. If a player interacts with it, they will be transported to a hallway where the fire exit is moving away from them and the walls are shrinking. Players reach and exit the fire exit at the end before being crushed. After escaping, the door cannot be interacted with anymore.

The Coffin that holds the reward.

One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn after opening the Coffin with a key.

The seat next to the Coffin will spawn a Gutting knife. Players must find the in-tact corpse of an employee nailed to wood in the interior and insert the knife into their stomach. Players must then repeatedly interact with the knife to open up the employees guts.

While the employee's guts fall out, a key will fall to the ground and a sound effect will play. Players can now return to and open the Coffin for their reward.

A cause of death will be written next to the Coffin. Players must remember this and make their way to one of the Morgues that has eight different trays to open. On the back wall will be an autopsy report for each person and players must open the tray of the named individual that best matches the cause of death description. If a player opens an incorrect tray, a black hand will reach out and crush its fist, dealing 666 damage to all nearby players including players in portions of adjacent rooms.

If players open the correct tray, a key will slide out instead and a sound effect will play. Players can now return to and open the Coffin for their reward.

Around the corner in the same room as the Coffin will be a device to place five fingers. Players must find three chairs in Padded Cells and sit in them. They can then repeatedly interact with the cranks on either side to drop a blade onto and slice off their own fingers, dealing 10 damage to themselves. Although players only need five fingers, they can only get out of a chair after slicing off both fingers.

Players can then return to and place each finger on the device. They will be prompted to interact with the screen above the device which will spawn the key to open the Coffin for their reward.

The reward is randomized, but the chance for a more valuable reward is increased by how early in the day players complete the objective and is influenced by the vanilla luck system. The value of the reward is additionally increased by a difficulty multiplier, ranging from 0.6x to 1.4x, and a solo (singleplayer) multiplier of 1.17x. Gut the Corpse is considered Easy difficulty and has a 1.0x multiplier, Discover the Body is considered Medium difficulty and has a 1.15x multiplier, and Pay in Blood is considered Hard difficulty and has a 1.4x multiplier. The base value and multipliers for objective rewards can be adjusted in the Wesleys Interior Tools config under the Secondary Objectives section.

Upon collecting any reward, Hailey Robertson, the woman in the Coffin, will begin haunting players. Spooky sound effects will randomly play followed by a message next to the player's stamina bar, which is Hailey Robertson speaking to them. This haunting persists across all moons barring moons like Galetry and Gordion.

Eventually, Hailey Robertson will announce her prescence with the player's screen turning red and getting a fear effect. This will spawn her as an actual entity, being a variant of the Ghost Girl. She will disappear upon returning to orbit. However, she can spawn once per reward grabbed and continue haunting players if multiple rewards are picked up. This can also apply if players pick up a medallion again after dropping it in the ship, typically after the save file is reloaded.

After Hailey Robertson spawns for the first time on that save file, players will receive a journal entry about her.

Text ⁠
HAILEY ROBERTSON

First name: Hailey
Last name: Robertson
Middle name: -

Gender: F
Age: 32

Occupation: Nurse
Establishment: Crosswind Mental Hospital
Place: Last Hope

Cause of death: Poisoning

Hailey Robertson was found deceased in the treatment room of the Crosswind Mental Hospital, She had signs of physical abuse, lacerations to the back and chest, and a small hole was discovered in her forehead.

A notebook was recovered from a burning bin containing a detailed log of the experiments she was put through. Among which were, being forcefully exposed to violent videos of human torture for days on end without breaks. Being suffocated to the edge of death causing minor brain damage. Having her solve complex logic puzzles within certain timeframes and being punished for failing.

She was often reminded how her four year old son would not be able to survive without her as she was a single mother. This was with the promise of her being let go if she complied.
Unfortunately he also died of starvation during her capture.

A tiny rod was used to destroy a small part of her brain which likely led to her losing any sort of self. This was one of the final experiments listed within the notebook.

Hailey Robertson was one of many victims of such experiments and life altering treatments by the hands of Solover Underhill, the head psychiatrist of the Crosswind Mental Hospital.

She was a loving, hard working mother who had a hard time following her husband’s passing. She was full of courage and remained positive even during her hardest times.
She will be remembered by all.
May she Rest in Peace.

—-----------------------------------------

An annotated and rough map of the Void Rooms.

The Void Rooms are accessed by walking into a pair of floating white eyes in the interior that disappear when a player gets close to them. If a player walks close enough to the eyes, they will be teleported straight down into a separate part of the interior. Although the Void Rooms almost always spawn, the floating eyes can sometimes spawn in walls and make them practically inaccessible. Multiple players can enter the Void Rooms, but they can not be accessed again after players leave them.

The Void Rooms are a large, dark, and maze-like recreation of the ordinary Rubber Rooms. Shadowy figures are present and watch the player, disappearing when a player gets close to them. Some objects and furniture also disappears upon getting close to them. Currently, the layout of the rooms is always the same but walls connecting or disconnecting some paths is random. Faint white lines on the floor can be used as navigation towards the exit, but can lead to dead-ends. The exit to the Void Rooms always generates in the library at the top left of the map.

When a player enters the Void Rooms, two Void-Heads will immediately spawn. This is a variant of the Coil-Head that does not move while in its patrolling state but behaves similarly otherwise. One Void-Head will spawn in the bottom right corner of the Void Rooms while the other will spawn in front of the exit door.

Additionally, the Void Rooms generates 11 Void Items. This scrap currently generates in the same locations, but the scrap itself is randomized. Any Void Items players collect are their reward for the event.

The moon of Selector houses an armory deep within its snowy peaks. Once used for storing various weaponry to aid in times of war now lies abandoned waiting to be opened once more.

POPULATION: Abandoned.

CONDITIONS: Cold, lush terrain, oxygen rich atmosphere.

FAUNA: FAUNA: A stable ecosystem, dominated by insects.

Selector is a hilly, snowy, and forested moon with mountainous terrain. Plant life is rather abundant in the form of tall grass, bushes, and trees. Several large and small rocks can be found on the exterior as well.

Its most prominent landmark the is the colossal concrete and metal building behind the ship. Two elevators to the left and right behind the ship can be interacted with to descend into a deep chasm with several stalactites and stalagmites. The main entrance and both fire exits can be found at the bottom leading into the building. A Log translator and Floppy disc machine can be found at the bottom as well.
Selector supports Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, Hurricane, or Minefield weather by default.

A Cache of scrap can be found northeast of the ship in a small patch of open terrain. This Cache will always spawn a Recovery order and will additionally spawn up to six random items from a pool of Cables, Circuit boards, Copper wiring, Lithium, Steel ingots, and at a much lower chance Triangulation devices. The Cache will reroll its generated items with each landing, so players can leave and return to Selector if they dislike the items on it. However, as soon as any player gets too close to the Cache it will only spawn the Recovery order on future landings on that save file.

If players decided to overload and blow up ResearcherxB, debris from the ship can fall to the left (north) of the ship on the exterior of Selector. If players land on Selector in the future on that save file, a mild outbreak of white mold will be present on the exterior and two Infected Bunker Spiders will spawn on the exterior at the start of the day.

The Skinned Thumper is a hostile entity and variant of the Thumper added by Wesley's Ememy Variants. As its name implies, it looks like a Thumper but has burnt, flayed, and red skin.

The Skinned Thumper behaves identical to the Thumper, rapidly accelerating while moving and decelerating when having to make turns while chasing a player. They spawn sequentially in the front-left, front-right, back-left, and back-right of the arena looking to the right, so players can wait behind where the Skinned Thumper will be spawned to avoid immediate detection and it will roam around aimlessly. However, it is often advised to be be seen by the Skinned Thumper to have more control over its movement.

Importantly, the Skinned Thumper has a Stun Time Multiplier of 1, meaning the base 2 second stun duration of the Advanced nightstick applies to the it. Typically the Skinned Thumper will break out of its stun after 3 hits for a brief second, so players should move slightly after each third hit to avoid accumulating damage and continue stunlocking it.

With the exception of the Flamethrower attack, many opporunities to attack a Skinned Thumper can be created either during or in-between The Exterminator's attacks with good positioning. The first Skinned Thumper can also be killed in one cycle before or right as The Exterminator is about to launch its first attack provided players immediately engage with it and do not miss a single hit.

Four Skinned Thumpers are dropped into the arena one-by-one after each one is killed during The Exterminator event in the Grand Armory. These spawns do no contribute to total Power Level, and the Max Count and Power Level of the Skinned Thumper only matter if players modify spawn tables to spawn the Skinned Thumper elsewhere.

The Smile is a hostile entity and variant of the Coil-Head added by Wesley's Ememy Variants. It has a purple body resembling that of a large disc with two legs and feet. As its name implies, it also has a wide, toothy smile and two red eyes, staring at players.

Behaviorally, the Smile is very similar to the Coil-Head, having the same patrolling state, attacking state, etc. However, the Smile is typically only visible when in close proximity to a player. The distance at which the Smile can be seen varies depending on the interior.

The Smile also moves significantly slower than the Coil-Head, barely keeping the same pace as players sprinting at around 50lbs while chasing them. The time it takes for the Smile to deactivate while actively moving towards a player is increased to around 30 seconds to compensate.

If the Smile is not currently being observed and comes into contact with a player, they will rapidly take 90 damage per hit. Any player that dies to the Smile will have their head pop off and replaced by a coil.

The Snatcher is a hostile entity and variant of the Thumper added by Wesley's Ememy Variants. It has an oval-shaped body comprised of a muddy-like substance similar to the sludge it resides in. It has several limbs and hands, two glowing eyes, and a mouth constantly spitting sludge onto the floor.

Not to be confused with the several other encounters players can have with the Snatcher in the Deep Sewers, the actual entity behaves similarly to a Thumper. It will roam around the interior until spotting a player to chase, rapidly accelerating while moving and decelerating when having to turn or after hitting a wall. It will deal 40 damage to players that come into contact with its main body. Due to the hitbox of the Snatcher being larger and higher up than the Thumper, it is more feasible, albeit still ill-advised, to fight and kill it with a knife.

The Snatcher has a 50% chance to spawn within the Deep Sewers at exactly 5pm. A roar can be heard at this time while in the interior as an indicator for it spawning. This spawn does not contribute to total Power Level, and the technical Max Count and Power Level of the Snatcher only matter if players modify spawn tables to spawn the Snatcher elsewhere.

Snatcher ⁠
SNATCHER

Sigurd's danger level: 65%

Scientific name: Mudcantis-suratin

The Mudcantis-suratin or more commonly known as the Snatcher is a part of the Uranuh family. It is a muddy creature which prefers warm, swampy areas where it is most commonly found. Female Snatchers tend to have a soft, muddy skin covered in tiny tendrils which are often mistaken for thick hairs. Male snatchers have a thick, hard calcium plate below their “face” under a thinner, rubbery layer of skin.

Snatchers have a great amount of appendages, growing more as they get older, ending in hand-like shapes. While they look like hands they only resemble them and do not contain any Intrinsic muscles. However these are very strong and are their main form of travel both underwater and on land.

Snatchers are not naturally aggressive creatures despite their intimidating look. They prefer to stick to the shadows or cloudy lakes and watch from a distance. The females are entirely herbivores while the males do snatch, drown and digest small creatures entirely for the calcium required to grow their face plate.

However it is not always safe to assume a snatcher won’t harm you. It will act in self defense if it feels threatened with measures ranging from spitting thick sludge at you to violently swinging its appendages at you.
This act of defense is also amplified, specifically in females if anyone or anything approaches their nesting area. Chasing down and often viciously killing those who get too close to her young.

The mating process of snatchers is often fatal for the male as it requires them to briefly suffocate within the female. On the occasion of death, the female will mourn the male in their own unique way. The male’s skin gets repurposed to create a softer bed for the eggs once they are eventually laid. While the face plate will be hidden somewhere deep underwater as a form of burial. They often visit the burial site and seek to protect it from any intruders.

While on the surface Snatchers are often described as monsters due to their name and look, they are very emotional and have a surprisingly good memory. There have been several counts of people befriending a Snatcher with them still remembering that person a decade later.

It is recommended to stay away from their nests and leave them be when encountered in the wild. While deaths by snatchers are not common, it is a possibility.

The moon of Spine is mostly oceanic, being covered in many smaller islands housing their own land based ecosystems. Due to the nature of the island's history it was found that the soil is greatly beneficial to the plants which root themselves in the dirt. The high concentrations of Haemoglobin in the environment from ancient leviathans making it their final resting place causing a slight discoloration witin the plants themselves.

POPULATION: Abandoned.

CONDITIONS: Warm, rich, high concentration of hemoglobin in local fosilised formations.

FAUNA: A stable ecosystem, dominated by insects.

Spine is an island surrounded by ocean. Most of the island is a tropical forest with several trees and foliage with an orangish tint, while outskirts of the island are sandy beaches with palm trees. True to its name, there also also several fossilized leviathan spines and ribcages scattered around the island. A colossal fossil can be seen southeast from the ship and can be walked on, though it leads nowhere.

Multiple bridges can be found on the exterior as well as three greenhouses, which are the main entrance and fire exits. Some of the aforementioned fossils can be used as bridges or staircases as well. The main entrance greenhouse can be accessed by going west and slightly south of the ship up a hill to a bridge, a fire exit is located far to the south and slightly to the west on the outskirts of the island, and the other fire exit is to the east on the beach.
Spine supports Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, Hurricane, and Minefield weather by default.
Spine does not contain any notable exclusive content or mechanics, though it does have the highest chance of spawning the Greenhouse interior alongside Faith.

• A Log translator can be found underneath the exterior. It is actually possible to reach it by going deep enough into the ocean to end up underneath the water layer, going far enough to where the plain of grass ends, and jumping off and jetpacking underneath the exterior back towards the island and underneath where the ship is. The interior can be accessed from the exterior by doing this as well.

The main entrance of the Spooky Manor.

The Spooky Manor, also referred to as the Dilapidated Manor, is a variation of the Mansion interior. It is similar in gameplay but is structurally distinct, has extra tiles, and has dramatically altered visuals to make it look older and more decrepit. It most commonly spawns on Crowd followed by Gloom. The former generates a unique trial there instead of a Secondary Objective.

• Attic - A small attic with several boxes and tools in it. A safe and painting are also here, which the safe requires a Manor safe key to open. A key is acquired after completing a Secondary Objective.
  • Dining Hall - A large hall with a fireplace with tables and silverware set up for a meal. This area is mostly for the Prepare for Dinner objective.
  • Library - A room with several bookshelves that is different from the larger room with a staircase and bookshelves. This area is mostly for the Pull the Books objective.
  • Wine Cellar - A narrow corridor that connects to a wine cellar.
  • Empty Pool - The pool room that normally has water and a pink inflatable in it can sometimes be empty.
• Moons tagged as RegularManor will switch to vanilla textures and visuals.

The painting and safe in the Attic.

One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that spawns in the safe located in the Attic.

The painting next to the safe in the Attic will tell players to find them inside the interior. Players must find the room in the interior with a painting that has glowing eyes. Players must then find and interact with a key lodged into the wall or floor in that room.

Once players get the key, they can return to and open the safe in the Attic for their reward.

If the painting next to the safe in the Attic is brown, players can find a similar painting above the fire place in the Dining Hall. There will be a set of two switches on the walls in each corner of the room with a hint above them. Players must turn off or on each light above a seat depending on how many guests, indicated by the plate in front of a seat having food on it, are in the room following the instructions of a hint. The simplified version of the hints are as follows:

  • If there are zero, one, or two guests, players must turn off all the lights.
  • If there are three or five guests, players must turn off the lights above the seat of each guest and turn on all other lights.
  • If there are four or six guests, players must turn on the light above the seat of each guest and turn off all other lights.
  • If there are seven or eight guests, players must turn on all the lights.

If successful, the fireplace will turn green and a key will be dropped out of it. Players can now return to the safe in the Attic and open it for their reward.

If the painting next to the safe in the Attic is of a clock with several books behind it, players can head to the Library and find a similar painting on the center pillar. Eight dark blue books with a yellow binding can be interacted with and moved on the bookshelves. Once a book is interacted with, a clock will start ticking and players must interact with all the books within about 35 seconds. Every book will reset after time is up.

If successful, the bookshelf behind the center pillar and painting will move and reveal the key. Players can now return to the safe in the Attic and open it for their reward.

The Springwater Hotfish is a docile entity and variant of the Backwater Gunkfish added by Wesley's Ememy Variants. It is a red stingray with two small eyes, five tentacles for its mouth, and a blue and greenish coloration around its eyes, on its back, and on its stinger.

Similar to the Backwater Gunkfish, the Springwater Hotfish will find a location to enter its hiding state near scrap, at an AI node, or near the closest player and can be heard flopping around while it does so. If any player enters its line of sight while it moves to this location, it will immediately stop moving and enter its hiding state.

After entering its hiding state, the Springwater Hotfish will remain there indefinitely if no players are in the interior or on the exterior where it is. If players are in the interior or on the exterior where it is, it will instead check for nearby players on a timer. If this timer runs out, it will get up, leave a small puddle of fiery goo behind, and find a new location to hide.

If a player steps on, hits, or remains too close to a Springwater Hotfish for too long, it will be frightened and spray all nearby players with goo that covers their visor. It will then flee, leaving behind a trail of slippery and fiery goo that lasts for the rest of the day. This goo deals 4 damage per hit to players standing anywhere on it except the outer edges, and the puddles can overlap to deal multiple instances of 4 damage at once.

Two universal bugs exist for the Backwater Gunkfish and all its variants. Firstly, all of them practically have 5hp instead of 4hp, as they only die after their hp drops below 0 rather than at 0. Secondly, all of them will use the same goo as whichever one first sprayed goo on a moon. While these differences are largely auditory or visual, the Springwater Hotfish can be made harmless or make every other Gunkfish harmful depending on which sprays its goo first.

The Springwater Hotfish has a chance to spawn on a few moons, most commonly spawning on Core.

Scientific name: Infectum linteum

The Backwater Gunkfish is a type of Gunkfish of the family Mobulidae. Unlike the other types of Gunkfish, the Backwater Gunkfish spends most of its time on land. It can inhabit any damp, warm space where a water source is present. Its body is fat, flat, squishy and gelatinous, the width of a doormat. Its tail, slightly harder than the rest of its soft body, can range from 2-3 feet in length. When stressed, its tail is often curled up over its head to position for firing mucus or to shake and rattle as a deterrent.

The Backwater Gunkfish feeds off organic material on surfaces, and for this reason, it is found most often around polluted water, swamps, or dirty sewers. When frightened, the Gunkfish can use an opening in its tail to release a burst of a thick, green mucus mixed with saliva to defend itself; the Backwater Gunkfish keeps an especially large "reserve" for emergency situations and can squirt multiple times. When needed, it uses part of this extra reserve to excrete from its body, increasing its mobility on land.

The Backwater Gunkfish is harmless and is considered a natural cleaner of its preferred environments. Its mucus is a disinfectant; though it is not safe or healthy to consume, it is unlikely to cause major harm if it enters the body through the eyes or nose. Its smell is often described as a mix of vinegar and lard, and it is slightly warm when freshly excreted.

Though not directly harmful, the Backwater Gunkfish is often considered a notorious pest to water treatment facilities and petroleum refineries. The gunkfish itself is evasive, capable of fitting itself into very small holes and pipes, and its mucus is arduous to remove once it has hardened, forming a substance comparable to ice. For all these reasons, the Backwater Gunkfish has lead to many accidents and should be taken seriously. Today, pest removal services are well-accustomed to safe Gunkfish removal and relocation operations, and there are many affordable options if you believe there is one in the area. The best way to prevent a Gunkfish infestation is to keep your environment clean and dry and to close off any access to standing water.

sections.html: Deep below the ocean waves lies a fortune long forgotten. The temple of Thalasso housed many of people we would now call ancient. They had their lifestyle, their rituals.. ones which are now deemed unnatural.

POPULATION: Died.

CONDITIONS: Ocean, diverse oceanic flora, high pressure.

FAUNA: A healthy ecosystem.

Thalasso can experience Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Forsaken, or Hurricane weather by default.

The path directly behind the ship leads to an intersection. The left path has moving walls in a pattern that push the player off onto the platform or the death pit below, with the pillars between the walls acting as safe zones. The right pathway has spiked walls that slam into the wall periodically and crush the player, with spaces in-between the walls acting as safe zones. A water tunnel is at the end of this path. Both paths lead to the main entrance.

Going to the path to left of the front of the ship, turning left, and continuing straight leads to the "drowning chamber" mentioned by the mysterious voice on Lecaro, which is also where a fire exit is. This chamber begins to fill with water when a player is at the bottom of it, and drowning can be avoided by either jumping on the pillars to escape or going into the fire exit.

Going to the path to the right of the front of the ship leads to an intersection. Continuing straight leads to a small entrance that leads to three crushers and another fire exit. There is a safe spot to stand in-between each crusher. From the fire exit door, it is possible to run straight through all three crushers without stopping with the full effects of the TZP-inhalant at 16lbs or less.

The path to the left at the intersection leads to a partially submerged chamber. A "Beholder's eye" can be placed on a pedestal to open the heart door in front of the pedestal. This leads to a hidden chamber with seven "Human heart" scrap on pedestals inside. On average, all seven hearts are a little over triple the value of one "Beholder's eye". Jumping prevents drowning and jumping onto objects can help recover stamina.

Thalasso's water level will begin to decrease at around 12:30PM and begin to rise again at around 07:30PM. This temporarily creates a new path that can be found by going to the path that is to the front left of the ship, turning left, and turning right instead of continuing straight. This leads to another fire exit previously only accessible with a cruiser (not recommended) or jetpack. This also temporarily gets rid of the water in the aforementioned chamber.
Interacting with the map found on the exterior of Lecaro.

Utril: Go to the path to the left of the front of the ship, turn left, and continue straight. This leads to the "drowning chamber" mentioned by the mysterious voice on Lecaro, which is also where one of the fire exits is. This chamber begins to fill with water when a player is at the bottom of it, and drowning can be avoided by either jumping on the pillars to escape or going into the fire exit. Once it's safe, there will be a hole to crouch into at the bottom of the chamber that leads to an interactable map. Interacting with this map will unlock Utril.

This map is hidden somewhere inside the temple of Thalasso. After interacting with it a strange audio will play. After that Utril will be unlocked for you.

Image & Text ⁠
Past the floating island, through two ravines they light the way, a guide through the darkness of Utril.

Image & Text ⁠
I am nearing my day of birth yet again. It will be the twenty first.
While to most it would seem a day of happiness.\nI look at it the opposite.
This year I have graduated for a course I was happy to start.
But time has shown that it might not be within my interest in this form.
Therefor I feel a part of life was wasted. I have yet to understand what I truly want to do with the years that remain.
I feel like a rock in a river. With life flowing around me. Unmoved. Waiting for change. Change that might never come if I stay this way.

Image & Text ⁠
During my time in this realm of mortality I have made friends of many. Though very few have stuck with me past my time of being around them.
Grateful I am to those who remain. Those whom I can consider close.
True friends.
However I fear that the friends I have made in the past year become one with those who no longer seek contact with me. The thought haunts me daily. I fear that I might end up alone once more.
I fear the void we call loneliness.
Often I sit down, just me and my thoughts. No one to join my pondering. To fill up the void.

Image & Text ⁠
It was a while ago when I first felt it. I felt it for a friends. But for the three years I was around. I was too scared to say something. And now we talk no longer.
I often wonder what life would be had I been more courageous.
But now I have felt it once more.
Someone else. Another friend.
But it is different this time. While I send it from my side. I know I will never receive it.
While to some it is a blessing. To me it is a curse. I feel the weight on my chest whenever I mention it.
I feel like I am driving them away whenever I send it.
I am lost.
And I do not know the way.

Image & Text ⁠
My existence, my being, my mortality are comming thougts which cycle through my head more often than not.
My future, my past, my heart's desires. And the choices made which brought me here. Could I have done something different I wonder. Could I have been happy.

I offered to have my heart cut out. In the ceremony of this rotation.
I hope to be placed among the others. I hope to be happy. I hope to be unalone.
I hope for my soul to be at peace within it. And may I be found.
I ask, please, take care of me.

The Wail is a hostile entity and variant of the Bracken added by Wesley's Ememy Variants. It is a pale floating head with hollowed out eyes, long black hair, and a fleshy appendage where its neck should be.

Similar to the Bracken, The Wail will silently stalk players and attempt to sneak up behind them to snap their neck with its long hair. If a player spots The Wail within the middle of their screen, it will be startled, begin to move towards its chosen room, wait, and repeat the whole process. Staring at The Wail increases the likelihood of it attempting to chase and attack the closest employee, and directly attacking The Wail instantly triggers this.

Any player that comes into contact with The Wail will be killed and it will attempt to drag their corpse to its chosen room. There currently is a bug where The Wail can take double damage, making it possible to instantly kill it with any form of double-barrel shotgun and do upwards of 8 damage per shot with a Single-barrel shotgun.
The Wail immediately spawns in the interior upon landing on a moon during Forsaken weather. This spawn does not contribute to the Interior Power Level of a moon.

The Toy Face Jester is a hostile entity and variant of the Jester added by Wesley's Ememy Variants. It looks the same as the Jester save for the skull being replaced with a large white face with two hollowed out eyes and an o-shaped mouth.

Unlike the Jester, the Toy Face Jester will almost immediately enter its chasing state after spawning in regardless of if it sees a player or not. It will chase the closest player and kill them on contact. However, its maximum speed is significantly reduced, only slightly outspeeding players that are walking.

After all players leave the interior, the Toy Face Jester will return to its boxed state and begin roaming around to find players. The Toy Face Jester has a following and cranking timer of 1 second, meaning it will almost immediately enter its chasing state upon seeing a player again.
The Toy Face Jester is spawned about 30 seconds after the Pink Apparatus is pulled in the Toy Store. This spawn does not contribute to total Power Level.

The main entrance of the toy store interior.

The Toy Store is a toy store themed interior that most commonly spawns on Filitrios.

• Toy Store - The primary area of the interior featuring carpeted floors, several tables and shelves, etc. Scrap can primarily spawn on the tables and shelves or in Chests.
  • Toy Vault - A large door with a large disturbed mask on it and symbols below it. Typically spawns close to or loosely connected to the main entrance. The vault can be or will be opened after completing a Secondary Objective and reveal a chest behind it with a reward.
  • Mask Room - Either a room with masks on the wall above the Ball Pit or hallways with several masks on the wall, though they typically spawn together.
  • Chest Gauntlet - A room with several Trapped Chests lining either said of the walkway that lead to a single interactable Chest. Interacting with this chest will cause the Trapped Chests to start activating from the first chest to the hallway entrances. Note that some chests may spring open early and players must wait at the intersection before quickly choosing a safe path to run down.
  • Wooden Labyrinth - A wooden area in the Toy Store that is older, more decrepit, and maze-like in structure. Several Nutcracker statues are scattered around in it.
  • Web-Wire Room - A room covered in cobwebs. This is primarily for the Avoid the Wires objective.
  • Pink Apparatus - A room that is not guaranteed to spawn that has a face and a Pink Apparatus as the nose. It is conductive, is two-handed, weighs 31lbs, and is worth ▮110. After taking the Pink Apparatus, music will begin playing, the face will get angry, the eyes will begin to glow red, and a shotgun will replace the nose and fire forward. A Toy Face Jester will also be spawned about 30 seconds after the apparatus is pulled.
  • Apparatus - A regular apparatus can spawn on a wooden tile, typically connected to or in the Wooden Labyrinth.

• Chests - Chests can be interacted with and opened, sometimes containing scrap inside them. However, these can also be Trapped Chests.
  • Carousel - A carousel players can ride on.
  • Players can interact with some of the masks on the wall to reveal graffiti behind them.
  • Nutcracker statues will be present on the exterior of a moon that spawns the Toy Store interior.

• Trapped Chests - Chests that jumpscare the player by springing out a mask attached to a coil after being opened, which is harmless. However, masks that spring out that are glowing red will shortly explode after the chest is opened and deal 65 damage to all nearby players.
  • Ball Pit - A bottomless ball pit. Any who jump inside will instantly die and cannot be recovered.
  • Tripwire Traps - A tripwire that triggers a shotgun. Any player coming into contact with the tripwire string will trigger it. All nearby players will take 99 damage and it will hurt or kill nearby entities. These can be disarmed by interacting with them. Note that these traps can spawn at fire exit doors.
  • "Welcome Home" Trap - A variant of the Tripwire Trap that only spawns in doorways with eight shotguns pointing down and one pointing through the doorway. If the trap is triggered, players can quickly interact with the trap weight on the side before it falls down to disable it. Another way to avoid taking damage from this trap is to sprint through it and run quickly to the left or right before the final shotgun can go off. Players hit by the trap will take 200 damage and it can hurt or kill entities.
  • Toy Face Jester - About 30 seconds after the Pink Apparatus is pulled, this variant of the Jester will spawn. It will almost immediately enter and exit its cranking state to begin pursuing players. However, it has a significantly reduced maximum speed.

The Toy Vault that holds the reward.

One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that spawns in the chest inside the Toy Vault.

If the Toy Vault has a symbol of a Nutcracker and key, players must find and kill the Key Wielding Nutcracker that almost immediately spawns in the interior upon landing. This is a variant of the Nutcracker with the only notable differences being the visuals. It will drop a Bloody shotgun, Bloody Ammo, and a Toy vault key on death.

Once the key is acquired, players can return to the Toy Vault, open the door, and open the chest for their reward.

If the Toy Vault has a symbol of a comedy and tragedy mask pointed to a direction, players must find a total of eight mask statues in the interior. They must be turned to face the respective listed direction depending on if they have a comedy or tragedy mask on them. These statues appear in sets of four and typically spawn in Toy Store sections of the interior as well as on staircases. If a statue's starting position is already facing the correct direction, it must be fully turned around back to that position to properly register for the objective.

After all eight statues are turned to face the correct direction, a sound effect will play and players can return to the Toy Vault to open the chest for their reward.

If the Toy Vault has a symbol of a button, players must head to the Web-Wire Room to push the button. There will now be several Tripwire Traps in the room that are difficult to discern from the webs. Players must carefully navigate through to the other side of the room, typically on the right-hand side, and push the button.

After the button is pushed, a sound effect will play and players can carefully leave the Web-Wire Room and head back to the Toy Vault to open the chest for their reward.

The reward is randomized, but the chance for a more valuable reward is increased by how early in the day players complete the objective and is influenced by the vanilla luck system. The value of the reward is additionally increased by a difficulty multiplier, ranging from 0.6x to 1.4x, and a solo (singleplayer) multiplier of 1.17x. Kill the Key Keeper and Turn the Masks are both considered Medium difficulty with a reward multiplier of 1.15x. Avoid the Wires is considered Hard difficulty and has a reward multiplier of 1.4x. The base value and multipliers for objective rewards can be adjusted in the Wesleys Interior Tools config under the Secondary Objectives section.

The Cake prior to starting the event.

The Cake can randomly spawn within the interior. It is a room with a large cake roughly in the center of the room that prompts players to eat it. If a player interacts with the cake, the walls will slide over all four sides of the room and trap all players inside. Music will begin playing, the room will begin spinning, and a head with two masks will spring out of the top of The Cake.

Five waves of shotguns starting from the second layer and ending on the first layer of The Cake will start appearing and firing. These deal 200 damage per hit and are angled to hit all players in front of them. There are specific patterns The Cake chooses from for these waves of shotguns, but which pattern is chosen is random.

Before the start of the third wave, two spinning blades will come out of The Cake. Coming into contact with the sharp end of the blade will deal 100 damage to players. Additionally, four knives that rotate around the edge of the arena will appear during the third wave that also deal 100 damage to players that come into contact with their sharp edge.

After all five waves, the walls will slide back open and players must immediately run out of any door and away from the room. The Cake will shortly explode after the fifth wave and rapidly deal 20 damage per hit to any players nearby. Players can safely return to the room after the explosion, but note that the knives are still present and still deal damage to players that walk into them.

The reward for the event is seven scrap that spawns where The Cake was. This seven scrap is randomly selected from the moon's scrap table. Note that this scrap only spawns if the player that initially interacted with The Cake survives until it explodes and that specific player is not teleported via the ship's vanilla teleporter. Additional modification to teleport a player through other means is generally fine.

• The Cake existed prior to the Obscurity update and is now considered its interior event. The four knives that rotate around the edge of the arena also previously only spawned during Eclipsed weather.
  • A spooky version of the Toy Store created for Halloween can be enabled in the Magic Wesley Toy Store config.

sections.html: Once a thriving moon clustered with many cities, Trite was the place to be. However deep into the war there was a catastrophic attack, leaving the cities in ash. Many had fled and left their stuff behind. But it is still riddled with remants of war.

POPULATION: Destroyed.

CONDITIONS: Warm, desert terrain, covered in ash.

FAUNA: A destroyed ecosystem.

Unfinished Section

Trite environment
Trite can experience Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, Hurricane, or Minefield weather by default.
On Trite you can hear two ambiences. One plays inside while the other one plays outside.

Trite's exterior has 57 turrets that spawn immediately in set locations. A turret in an alley connected to a path directly behind the ship is immediately active upon landing.

The rest of these turrets are activated by triggering a Scanner. This is a map hazard attached to metal poles on the exterior. When a player walks near one or at a specific position near one, it will drop down and turn on a red search light that patrols the area in a back-and-forth motion. Any player that walks into this search light will make the light turn green and activate several nearby turrets for the rest of the day.

Trite's interior has a unique map hazard called a Lone listener. They can be heard constantly playing music throughout the day to indicate their position. When a player is alone and approaches a listener, it will play a voiceline, play its music at a lower pitch, turn on its light, and begin tracking the player for about 10 seconds. If the player makes any noise during this time, such as talking, walking, etc., the listener will attempt to flash the player with its light and rapidly deal 999 damage per hit. This flash can be obstructed with walls, can be triggered through walls, and makes the listener inactive for the rest of the day. If the player does not make noise during this time, the listener will go back to playing its normal music and repeat the process when another lone player gets close to it.

Trite has a lone interior fire exit that leads to the top of the right skyscraper. It is technically possible to get to this fire exit with a jetpack from the exterior, but it is ill-advised to attempt doing so. Dropping items at this high of an altitude will suspend them in the air, so this fire exit should be primarily used as a last resort for escaping. Players can use a Health-stim to overcap their hp and survive the fall from the top of the skyscraper. Walking or jumping straight off from the edge of the fire exit will have the player end up nearby if not directly on the ship.

To the north and slightly east of the ship is a building that can either randomly fall or can be triggered to fall by a player that interacts with it for about 120 seconds. Either way, the building will begin to fall forward into another building and cause a domino effect of moving several buildings. After about 60 seconds the building south of the ship will begin to move and crash onto the ground next to the ship if the building randomly started falling or almost onto the ship itself if a player triggered the fall, dealing 200 damage to any player underneath it. The ship will take off and return to orbit to avoid being crushed by the building if a player triggered the fall.

sections.h: Major Story Spoilers: Decision or Failure Aftermath
sections.html:
If players decided to not overload and blow up ResearcherxB or otherwise did not successfully locate the ship, players will receive a distress signal that tells them their time is up and that ResearcherxB will crash onto Trite. ResearcherxB will become inaccessible on that save file past this point. The next time players land on Trite, they will receive a signal, usually in the afternoon, that the ship is about to crash. The ship will then crash onto Trite's exterior in roughly another hour of in-game time.

If players land on Trite in the future on that save file, it will have been completely overrun by white mold. Several Infected Bunker Spiders will spawn on the exterior immediately upon landing and large portions of the interior will be covered in growth, obscuring vision.

Trite was a thriving and powerful moon in the region under the rule of the Emperor. However, the Triton military's destruction of Calist was the catalyst for a war that eventually lead to Trite being bombarded and decimated by opposing dominions.

Radio message 3 continues the story of the Across the Stars radio host, unlocking Filitrios when logged. They cover the fall of Trite and recommed to head to Demetrica.

Text ⁠
This is
-Across The Stars-
Back with the 11-ish AM news, I’m a little late today.
There’s a lot to catch up on nowadays.
It’s been a cloudy week and it looks like it’ll be cloudy for a little while longer.

The reports have not been great.. quite the opposite in fact.
If you haven’t heard it already, Trite has suffered its most devastating attack yet.
..The cities have fallen.
I’ll repeat it once more, the cities of Trite have fallen.
According to my sources most of the people were able to flee in time.
I wish I could say I know what will happen next.
But..
I can’t.
What the Triton Military will do next is a mystery.

All I can say is go to the Domes of Demetrica, and survive.

There will be some comforting tunes, please, stay tuned.
And for those still listening, thank you.

sections.html: Utril, home of the Spore Lizards, infested with arachnids. This moon is home to a research lab where they dabbled into the cloning of wildlife. To better harvest the goodies from the Spore Lizards. Every science has its risks however.

POPULATION: Executed.

CONDITIONS: Dark, dry terrain, poisonous atmosphere populated by Lycoperdon perlatum.

FAUNA: A flawed ecosystem, home to Lacerta-glomerorum, dominated by arachnids.

Unfinished Section

This section seems unfinished. If you're a wiki editor, please help with completing this section.

Utril's flora consists of larger Pyntrus Lotuses and Puffbulbs. Similar to Spore Lizards and the scrap, approaching the Puffbulbs will release a temporary purple cloud that obscures player vision.
Utril can experience Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Flooded, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, or Hurricane weather by default.

On the path to the main entrance, a map can be found that reads "Do not touch or hit these trees". Two trees can be located on this same path marked by an X on the map, one being directly behind the map, and can be hit with a shovel or knife. Hitting both trees will collapse the platform above the main entrance, crushing any player underneath it. This allows for easier traversal to the fire exit on top of the platform without needing to climb a vine (ladder) or use other tools. The main entrance is still accessible through a small crack behind the fire exit building and it is possible to get back up. However, it is recommended to exit through a fire exit or use an extension ladder to get back up due to the difficulty at higher weights.

Utril's interior features a unique map hazard called an "Acid Tank". If any injured player walks underneath this tank, it will begin spraying acid for about 12 seconds in a small area. Additionally, a puddle of acid will form below the tank and linger for roughly 70 seconds after the tank has finished spraying. Both the acid spray and puddle deal 5 damage per hit to any player standing inside of them, but the puddle deals damage at a slower rate. The puddle will still be visible but not deal any damage to the player after this timeframe.

Utril's exterior also has an altar where a mysterious object can be placed. To reach it, run up the hill behind the ship, turn left, and run along the right wall. This mysterious object is a Brooding seed that can be found in a hidden chamber on the exterior of Berunah. Placing the seed will cause a warning message to appear that says "A Cosmic Entity of unknown power has turned it's focus towards this planet."

This dramatically alters the terrain on the exterior, causes several tentacles to appear on the exterior that deal 20 damage per hit on contact, visually alters the interior, and causes the Assimilated Growth to almost immediately spawn in the interior when landing on the moon in the future. All these changes also apply to Vindict.

This persists until players are fired unless seeds are also placed on the exteriors of Etern, Filitrios, Fission-C, and Gloom, in which case these changes become permanent on that save file.

If players decided to overload and blow up ResearcherxB, debris from the ship can fall onto Utril's exterior. If players land on Utril in the future on that save file, a mild outbreak of white mold will be present on the exterior and Infected Bunker Spiders will spawn on the exterior at the start of the day.

Interacting with the map found on the exterior of Thalasso.
Alternatively, inserting the Utril videotape that randomly spawns as scrap within the interiors of Cosmocos, Desolation, Gloom, or Gratar into the projector in Galetry.

Cubatres: Find the fire exit that's besides the test tubes. Follow that path that goes down and keep an eye on an opening on your right. In the opening you will find a map drawn on the ground. Interacting with this will cause a short cutscene then unlock Cubatres.
Filitrios: Filitrios videotape that randomly spawns as scrap within the interior.
Desolation: Log "Harrington's Crash Log" that randomly spawns as scrap within the interior.
End: Acquire the destiny item "Harrington's research 4" that randomly spawns as scrap within the interior and insert it into the destiny item slot before taking off in the abandoned ship on Repress.
Vindict: Vindict videotape that spawns randomly as scrap within the interior.
