sections.h: Harrington's Crash Log & Harrington's Research Logs
sections.html: Harrington's Crash Log and Harrington's research can spawn randomly as scrap within the interior and continue the story of Professor Harrington, a scientist previously researching on Cosmocos before its split and teleportation. After leaving the split chunk of Cosmocos that came to be known as Desolation, Harrington crash landed on either an undisclosed location or Utril itself and aided in major breakthroughs in the cloning process after recovering. Once the military got involved, Professor Harrington sabotaged the project by removing any mention or research of a chemical that prevents clones from dying of cancer in about a month.

Text ⁠
The past few weeks have been difficult.
My memory hasn't been the same since the crash.
I do not recall much from before.
All that remains is some faint visions of self healing flesh, independently growing eyes and a bright flash before panic ensued.
4 of us fled to one of ships and escaped the scene.
I don't know what happened to the other two teams who were present at the time.
I have now come to know that the entirety of Cosmocos vanished. And what we were standing on was merely a severed chunk of it.

Nobody has dared to return. We called it Desolation.
I'll attach the coordinates to this log for anyone brave enough to have a look for themselves.
After my recovery I might be able to help the people out over here.
I've heard some interesting projects being discussed.

Professor Harrington, over and out.

Text ⁠
It's been a while now since my arrival at this facility.
I've been closely paying attention to the projects here.
I was told that moon is THE home of the Lacerta-glomerorum.
Or.. spore lizards in the common tongue.
This is where they are most frequently hunted.
However, in the labs they seem to be working on cloning technology.
The cloning of creatures to be more specific.
I feel it's right up my alley.
Professor Harrington, over and out.

Text ⁠
I wanted to give an update to my time here.
The cloning process is very complex but the technology is easy to produce.
When they explained to me the current state of the project I was told that they had figured out how to grow a spore lizard from practically nothing to a fully functioning adult in the matter of days.
However there was one fatal flaw.
Due to GYN-H chemicals used in the process of speeding up the development of the creature, a unique form of cancer would grow in the brain which, after about a month would kill it.
But I think I came up with a solution, LYN-H is a very similar chemical to GYN-H, It's only down one component.
I've theorised this could be the required change.
Professor Harrington, over and out.

Text ⁠
Not weeks ago we had a big breakthrough with one of my theories.
Now yesterday our front door was broken though.
After having celebrated our victory in the cloning of spore lizards we weren't expecting to see the military show up to investigate our lab.
But after learning about our success in the cloning department, we had a.. less than peaceful discussion as they had brought it to their higher ranks who now demand to use it to clone.. people.. for the war of course.
This leaves us with a choice, we either give them an unlimited army.. or we destroy all our progress.

I have to take my leave.
Professor Harrington, over and out.

Text ⁠
This will be my last day here, after today, I will be fleeing once more.
But to someplace safe this time.
We had come to the decision that the decades of research was simply too valuable to destroy.
So we have handed them the tools, the research and they will likely proceed with making their own soldier in labs.
The prospect of that is horrifying.
Or.. well
It would have been had I not removed any mention of LYN-H, the one thing that prevents clones from dying shortly after being created.
The armies they grow will all drop dead within a month after being created.
Time to find a brighter horizon.
Professor Harrington, over.. and out.

Somewhere on moon's exterior there's a hidden map on the ground that you can interact with. When you proceed to do so a strange audio will play. After that Cubatres will be unlocked for you.

Image & Text ⁠
Out in the unknown, the light shines in mysterious ways, beauty you willl find before death takes you away.

If the player randomly finds Utril's videotape in the interior of other moons and inserts it into the projector in Galetry, Professor Harrington will also describe the environment of Utril.
This videotape can be found on Gloom, Gratar, Desolation and Cosmocos.

Text ⁠
I really am cursed to live out my days recording with subpar recording devices.

This is professor Harrington and I have found myself to be on Utril.
The days may be darker than the nights yet it has a strange sense of beauty.
It is not a place I ever expected to visit.
The wildlife is unlike the usual, not very diverse.
Generally consistent of spore lizards and arachnids.
It was surprising to learn that it wasn't the spiders that were the aggressive ones here.
They were much more keen on posing for a picture.
Either way,
I'm needed back in the labs.
Professor Harrington, over and out.

This page is under constructon! It's not supposed to be linked anywhere. You can help finishing this page if you trully want to.

The area named Vindict residing on the moon of Utril is known for its extremely hazardous infestation of White mold. It is recommended to stay clear from this area. The I.T.D.A. has decided to contain it rather than attempt clearing it. Visit at your own risk. Medical equipment remains inside.

POPULATION: Executed.

CONDITIONS: Bright, dry terrain, poisonous atmosphere with high mold density.

FAUNA: FAUNA: A flawed ecosystem, home to Lacerta-glomerorum, dominated by arachnids.

Vindict is a hilly and grassy moon with bridges to get across a valley. It has several small and large twisted tree formations. The flora consisting of Pyntrus Lotuses, tall bushes and grass, and other dead trees has been completely overrun by the white mold and has a white coloration to it. Eight sets of strange red eggs can also be found scattered around the exterior.

Three concrete buildings can be found on the exterior, which are the main entrance and fire exits. The main entrance is atop a hill and is visible northwest of the ship. Both fire exits are to the left and right respectively in the valley behind and west of the ship.
Vindict supports Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, and Hurricane weather by default.

Vindict's exterior has spikes of white mold on the that will continously and rapidly deal 4 damage to any player that gets in close proximity of them.

Vindict's interior has similar spikes, but they only pulse once and deal 10 damage. They can hit a player twice if a player moves back into the spike during a pulse animation. Mold is also abundant in the interior and can greatly hinder visibility.

In the valley behind and west of the ship is a Databox and Cache. This Cache will always spawn a Recovery order and will additionally spawn up to six random items from a pool of Cables, Circuit boards, Copper wiring, Lithium, Steel ingots, and at a much lower chance Triangulation devices. The Cache will reroll its generated items with each landing, so players can leave and return to Vindict if they dislike the items on it. However, as soon as any player gets too close to the Cache it will only spawn the Recovery order on future landings on that save file.

If a Brooding seed was placed on the altar on the exterior of Utril, the terrain on the exterior will be dramatically altered, several tentacles will appear on the exterior that deal 20 damage per hit on contact, the interior will be visually altered, and an Assimilated Growth will almost immediately spawn in the interior when landing on Vindict in the future. This persists until players are fired unless seeds are also placed on the exteriors of Etern, Filitrios, Fission-C, and Gloom, in which case these changes become permanent on that save file.

Transcript security recording - Day 14 
------------------------ 15:12 - Cargo dock

C. Darter: That’s everything in cargo?
S. Dent: Just about, yeah.
C. Darter: Good, I’ll signal Julian so he can start the engines.
S. Dent: He knows how to fly this thing? I thought he was only here in case things like.. that.. Jump out on us.
C. Darter: He doesn’t need to know how to fly, the autopilot takes care of that. He only needs to power the engines and make sure nothing goes up in flames in the process.
S. Dent: oh, I assumed there was some manual labour involved in the taking off part but that makes sense. Well I’ll be in the office on Level 2 documenting our discoveries.
C. Darter: Alright.

------------------------ 17:20 - Central hallway

S. Dent: Hey, is everything in order?
J. Charter: I have nothing to report on, there hasn’t been a breach of containment.
S. Dent: That’s good.
J. Charter: Sorry for asking but, what is that stuff we collected?
S. Dent: It’s a type of Eumycota.. or fungi in layman's terms, a white mold that seems to form these spike-like pustules which it uses to inject itself into any unfortunate creature that happens to step on it.
J. Charter: I see. So that’s what was wrong with that spider.
S. Dent: Yeah, so don’t touch the mold.
J. Charter: What are you planning on doing with it?
S. Dent: That is classified.
J. Charter: Understood.
S. Dent: I’ve got some work to do so I’ll be off.
J. Okay. Stay safe.

------------------------ 22:43 - Communications

S. Underhill: What’s the status.
C. Darter: We have contained some new samples for the project.
S. Underhill: Is it promising?
C. Darter: ..Potentially, I have not conducted extensive research just yet.
S. Underhill: That will be your priority from now on.
C. Darter: Of course. As you wish.
S. Underhill: I sense that you are displeased. Is there anything I should know about?
C. Darter: It doesn’t feel right. It’s immoral. We shouldn’t build a future on the torture of innocents.
S. Underhill: If the loss of innocent lives worries you then I would recommend reminding yourself that our sins are as many as the others.
C. Darter: It isn’t right.
S. Underhill: Perhaps you don’t understand.
C. Darter: Understand what? The fact that innocent people are being cut to pieces for an opportunity of finding someone who we then also torture with the notion of it will help build our future? You mean that?
S. Underhill: We have our projects, our corporations, people, governments, ideologies, politics, empires.. together it forms a society.. The people strive to climb higher, rule, gain control, to sit at the top of whatever they feel gives them power, yet even when they get there, they still feel it.. that entity looming over their shoulder from a step on the ladder too high for anyone to reach. They hide behind the facade of smaller corporations. You know their influence. They allow us to exist as long as we provide, no matter the methods or the cost. If they won't care, why should we.
C. Darter: The.. entity?
S. Underhill: I expect a report tomorrow before the end of the day. Otherwise you will be considered for repurposing.
C. Darter: ..Understood.

The Void-Head is a hostile entity and variant of the Coil-Head added by Wesley's Ememy Variants. It is a floating, pitch black head with two glowing white eyes and a glowing mouth. It will shut its eyes and mouth when being observed or when deactivated.

Unlike the Coil-Head, the Void-Head does not move while in its patrolling state. It will simply wait until a player enters its line of sight before entering its attacking state. As such, one of the most effective strategies to deal with them is to lure them into an area players will not need to return to and deactivate them.

The Void-Head is similar in behavior otherwise, attempting to attack the closest player when no player is observing it. It has the same deactivation and reactivation timers as well. Any player that comes into contact with a Void-Head while it is not being observed will rapidly take 90 damage per hit, having their head popped off and replaced with a coil if they die.

Two Void-Heads will immediately spawn in the Void Rooms event in the Rubber Rooms after any player enters them through the floating eyes. They always spawn in the same two locations: the bottom right of the map and the top left of the map at the exit door.

Wesley's Weathers adds 5 new weathers that can occur on most moons: Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, Hurricane and Minefield.

Earthquakes weather causes an earthquake to occur roughly every 220 seconds upon loading a moon. This equates to a little over five hours of in-game time on a moon with a regular day speed, so an earthquake will occur around 01:00pm, 06:00pm, and 11:00pm.

On the exterior, this is purely auditory and visual. In the interior, this causes the roof to collapse and crush any player caught underneath the falling rubble. The amount of damage dealt varies and where the rubble falls is random. Some of this rubble gets left behind as an obstruction that disappears after about 45 seconds.

Earthquakes weather has a default scrap amount multiplier of 1.1, slightly increasing the total amount of scrap initially spawned on the moon.
During earthquake weather you can sometimes hear ambiences. One on the exterior and the other one within interior.

Forsaken weather plays ambient music and causes a storm of raining blood to occur on a moon. It also causes Emma, "the forsaken child", to haunt players. For example, Emma sometimes will fly towards a player in the interior while screaming. These encounters with Emma are purely auditory or visual and not to be confused with the entity Emma.

Forsaken weather causes The Wail, a variant of the Bracken with 10hp, to immediately spawn in the interior when landing. Additionally, the entity Emma, which is a variant of the Ghost Girl, will spawn at exactly 02:00pm within the interior.

Forsaken weather has a default scrap amount multiplier and scrap value multiplier of 1.2, increasing the total amount of scrap initially spawned and the value of scrap on the moon.
During forsaken weather you can hear two ambiences: One plays on the exterior while the other one plays within interior.

Hallowed weather plays ambient music and causes candles, which can float throughout the day, and pumpkins to spawn as objects on the exterior. If the Spooky Manor interior is generated, candles, pumpkins, and skulls will additionally decorate the interior.

Hallowed weather spawns map hazards on the exterior referred to as "scrap head". It is a pale head attached to a metal pole that lays dormant atop a mound of scrap metal. A player approaching the scrap head in its dormant state will cause it to activate, turn on its left eye which will emit a red light, lock onto the player, and begin to track the player's position for about 6-7 seconds. If the player walks into the red light during this time, the scrap head will attempt to lunge forward and bite the player, dealing 99 damage on contact, roar, and return to its dormant state. If the player is not detected, it will return to its dormant state. The scrap head has a cooldown of about 28 seconds before it can activate again once it returns to its dormant state.

Hallowed weather injects the Arachnohead, Corpse Crawler, and Creaker into the Enemy Spawns (Interior) table of any moon experiencing it with a weight of 35, 28, and 9 respectively. Any current weights less than these weights will be overridden.

  • The Arachnohead is a variant of the Bunker Spider with 2hp that explodes on death.
  • The Corpse Crawler is a variant of the Spore Lizard that vomits out a Gore Spike, which acts as a hazard and pulses outward with spikes about every 8 seconds to deal 20 damage to nearby players.
  • The Creaker is a variant of the Nutcracker with alternative sound effects and scrap. It exclusively spawns during this weather.
During Hallowed weather you can hear ambience that plays during this weather.

Hurricane weather causes strong winds and heavy rain to occur on a moon. It also causes trees to fall from the sky on the exterior throughout the day, sometimes increasing in frequency and causing many trees to fall in quick succession. These trees will knock back the player if nearby and additionally deal 50 damage to the player if they are close to its impact. These trees will be left behind as obstructions for the rest of the day.

Hurricane weather typically spawns 8-9 scrap on the exterior immediately upon loading a moon, specifically around random outdoor AI nodes. It uses a separate Loot Table from the rest of the moon.

Scientific name: Vorictus-detoma

The Vorictus-detoma, garnered the name “Droop” due to its drooping appearance. Its arms, legs and neck are exceptionally long, likely due to the body deformation which happens in the process of a Droop’s creation.

The Droop is not officially classified as a non-human creature, while it no longer possesses the humanity it once did, it technically is still human. Only with the effects of prolonged exposure to V-Radiation.

V-Radiation is an incredibly rare phenomenon and has previously had very adverse and unexplainable effects on creatures and places, often leading to deformation and destruction. Sightings of V-Radiation were extremely rare up until the Grand war where it was occasionally used to cause mass destruction. However, even by supporters of the use of biological warfare, it was greatly frowned upon due to its cruel and otherworldly effects often rendering places uninhabitable.

While there have not been many encounters, the majority of the Droop were likely everyday civilians affected during the war.
Direct exposure to gamma or beta rays of V-Radiation vaporises the average unprotected human, leaving behind what can only be described as a shadow or a memory where they once were. It is not certain what exactly it is that they leave behind but it is thought to no longer be alive. However there have been rumors of these shadows stalking or moving in the dark.
When exposed to alpha rays of V-Radiation you won’t immediately notice any harmful effects aside from a slight headache or brief dizziness. But from the moment of exposure you have been infected with a unique type of radiation sickness. While it doesn’t break your DNA, it does change it which only becomes noticeable after a few days. Skin might start feeling heavy and organs might move around during a very painful process. If the infected is still alive 13 days past the first exposure, changes start happening to the brain, often noting highly irregular brainwaves. From this point onwards it is only a husk of its former self. While it is on a technical level not death, this is what we consider the moment of death. The person is unrecoverable and the body is deformed to an unrecognisable level where the skin and muscles resemble a droopy obsidian.

There has not been any research from this point onwards.

His crooked smile and those fiery eyes staring at me through the bushes, still covered in Jane's blood. I will never forget that face. Image & Text ⁠ I've been here for six weeks now. They told me there will be a retrial for my case! THANK GOD! Maybe this time they will actually have a close look at all the evidence I've provided. This also means I can FINALLY leave this place. Even if temporarily. We're also slowly being moved to another prison I've heard. I really hope it's a little nicer because I am SICK of waking up to a swarm of rats running around our cells. The activities here are horrible too. We can't even work out since most of the equipment is either broken or extremely dirty. They cleared out a couple cell blocks already. I think we might be next. This does mean I'll have to leave my notes here. I don't think I can sneak those with me. I will find justice for you Jane. I loved you. Alongside the Prisoner Notes, a Guard's Note can be found which explains the fate of all prisoners on Alcatras. Image & Text ⁠ This poor guy didn't deserve this. I wonder if there are any other innocent prisoners here. If I knew this I would've made sure he wasn't put with the others. But. We're all just following orders here. It's vile what we do here. Poor guy thought he'd be moved. We don't keep prisoners here. We kill them and turn their bodies into soil. Soil which is used to grow crops at an extraordinary rate. These crops are then sold back to the public. People would go crazy if they knew about this. I would too. But that's just our job. I hate it but.. it's how money gets made. Alcatras Alcatras Main
plain.p-arachnohead: The Arachnohead is a hostile entity and variant of the Bunker Spider added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is a pale, baby doll-like head attached to four mechanical legs. It has a right blue eye and a left green eye that emit a light and are constantly shfiting focus. Similar to a Bunker Spider, an Arachnohead will initially attempt to create a nesting area by placing several webs in the surrounding area and will typically stop if it encounters a player until line of sight is broken. Once all the webs have been laid down, the Arachnohead will find a spot to wait until one of its webs is triggered, a player walks underneath it, or it is attacked by a player. It will then pursue that player. If the head of an Arachnohead comes into contact with players, they will take 90 damage. Any player that dies to an Arachnohead in this way will be cocooned, hung from the ceiling, and only be recoverable via the teleporter. The Arachnohead additionally explodes on death. This explosion deals 50 damage to all nearby players or kills players and entities very close to the explosion. This explosion can set off nearby landmines, set off other Arachnoheads , and set Forest Keepers on fire. An Arachnohead is guaranteed to spawn after triggering a Teddy Bear on Filitrios . The Arachnohead is also injected into the Enemy Spawns (Interior) table of any moon experiencing Hallowed weather with a weight of 35, overriding the current weight if it is lower than that. The Arachnohead can also naturally spawn on the following moons: Moon Name Interior or Exterior Spawn Chance Gratar Interior 5.44% Carnate Interior 3.86% Hyx Interior 2.51% Gloom Interior 2.13% Filitrios Interior 1.69% Arachnohead ⁠ ARACHNOHEAD Sigurd's danger level: 35% Scientific name: Areck-hetoma Areck-hetoma or the “Arachnohead” are vicious devices designed to ensnare their targets with the intent to kill. It is theorised their original intended purpose was to act as a security device and scare off intruders when spotted. However it is certain their current purpose is to only act as a trap, an artefact of the war predating the quiet age. Their appearance is that of a teddy bear with a head resembling that of a baby doll. The teddy bear exterior is only there to conceal the machinery of the Arachnohead itself in its dormant state. Upon activation it starts a search for any nearby entities internally listed as enemy targets. When a target is spotted it leaves its teddy enclosure and uses a set of four hydraulic legs to chase its target. The internals of the head are often very haphazardly wired and it is not uncommon for the wrong wires to cross during an impact of blunt force causing a short circuit leading to a possibly explosive reaction. While it is a flaw in the original design, it was never resolved due to it being a very favourable feature when used in times of conflict. plain.p-art-gallery: The main entrance in the Art Gallery. Note how the door has transformed into a painting. The Art Gallery is a museum themed interior that most commonly spawns on Cubatres . It always has three floors, and the main entrance is always on the second floor. After stepping away from main entrance the door visually transforms into a painting. First Floor - The first floor has many statues of entities, moons, and display cases. Scrap can spawn in these display cases, which can be broken by interacting with them multiple times or hitting them with a shovel. Second Floor - The second floor is the painting gallery and scrap generally spawns on the tables or pedestals. There is an additional part of this area with a wooden floor and many statues of hoarding bugs. Third Floor - The third floor is a more expansive wooden storage area with various boxes, statues, paintings, etc. Scrap can spawn on the floor here. Cube Display - Several chairs lying in front of a display case with a device to input a code next to it. This room typically spawns adjacent to the main entrance and the display case holds the Secondary Objective reward. Elevators - Two elevators connect to all three floors and can be used to go between them. Music can be heard playing from the elevators when nearby to indicate their position. A player can drop down from one floor to the next and take 50 damage without using an elevator, but dropping from the third floor to the first floor deals 100 damage. Entities can travel between floors through the broken elevator shaft. Lasso Man Sighting - Occasionally brief visions of a Lasso Man may appear that fades out of view after a couple seconds or upon getting close to it. Breaker Box - The breaker box in the Art Gallery is always accompanied by the same text, and turning it off can cause some secrets to be revealed. Movable Painting - Some paintings can be moved to reveal scrap behind them. If the Breaker Box is turned off, the paintings that can be moved will have a large X on them. Fog Machine - A fog machine can be found in the interior, primarily on the second floor, and reduces visibility in the surrounding area. It can be disabled by interacting with it. Lasso - A lasso that falls and hangs from the ceiling swaying around, dealing 666 damage to any player that walks into it and hanging them. Their corpse will be left hanging from the ceiling afterward. Mysterious Painting - Lasso Man will stalk players and appear in paintings they were last around or are currently near. He starts at the back of the painting and quickly moves forward to be front and center of it, accompanied by a sound effect. If a player makes too much noise near the painting, Lasso Man will lash out of it with long, sweeping tendrils that deal 666 damage to players if they come into contact with the ends of them. Lasso Man will then shortly retreat back into the painting and disappear. A close-up of The Painting attached to the wall after having broken its glass display case. The Painting serves as the apparatus for the interior, but it is not guaranteed to spawn. It is worth ▮220, is two-handed, and weighs 31lbs. It can be found in a glass casing at the end of a large room with several chairs, two Lasso Man statues, and a clock. This room always generates on the second floor. When a player enters this room, an alarm will go off, sets of lasers will appear, and the clock will start ticking from 12 o'clock. A player must reach the end of the room and retrieve The Painting without being detected by the lasers and within about 90 seconds. If a player is detected or time runs out, The Painting can no longer be grabbed and will shortly be shredded. If a player successfully grabs The Painting, it will trigger all apparatus related events. Players can safely stand between each set of lasers. On the left side of the room there is a note that provides instructions on how to move between the sets of lasers without being detected. When the lasers blink once, the lasers will shortly disappear and make it safe to move. When the lasers blink twice, it is not safe to move as the lasers disappear and reappear too quickly. When the lasers blink three times, it is not initially safe to move when the lasers briefly disappear but is safe to move the second time they disappear. At the beginning, players can hug the wall to get to the center pathway and avoid having to deal with the chairs. Players should then get as close to each set of lasers as possible to make it easier to safely get between them. Although it can be difficult to discern between two or three blinks, it is very easy to tell when one blink happens and the timing for moving for one or three blinks is rather forgiving. Additionally, players should make sure to be checking their backs for entities, as they can come into the room. The Cube Display that holds the reward with the device to input the code next to it. One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn inside the Cube Display . After turning off the breaker box, four symbols will appear at the bottom of the Cube Display . Players must wander around the Second Floor and find those four symbols with a number nearby. Players must then return to the Cube Display and input the numbered code matching the symbol code. If successful, a sound effect will play and the Cube Display will open for players to ge their reward. If players turn off the breaker box, they'll receive a hint at the bottom of the Cube Display to find a tower. This tower is a moving pillar with several hoarding bugs on the First Floor . The hoarding bugs with an X on them can be interacted with to turn them around and reveal a paper attached to their back. One of the papers will have the code written on it. After players learn the code, they can return to the Cube Display , input the code, and get their reward. If players turn off the breaker box, they'll receive a hint at the bottom of the Cube Display to find a vault. This vault spawns on the Second Floor in the area with wooden tiles. The vault will have three small dials and one large dial on it. Players must repeatedly turn the small dials until they hear a noticeably different click sound. Once all three small dials are in place, players must look at what numbers they point to and add them together. The larger dial must then be turned to that number. For example, if the three small dials point to 5, 10, and 20 respectively, the large dial must be turned to 35. Players can then repeatedly interact with the door handle to try and open the door. If successful, the door light will turn green and swing open to reveal the code. Players can then return to the Cube Display , input the code, and get their reward. The Lost Corridors can generate connected to the Second Floor . The entrance is a door with an outline of Lasso Man above it. Behind the door is a staircase that leads into a maze with statues of Lasso Man , various boxes, etc., scattered around. The general layout of the maze is always the same but what pathways are open or blocked off is random. Players must find their way through the maze to a door at the end of it. This door can be locked, but a key spawns next to it. Inside the room will be a painting with Lasso Man in it as well as a Crystal of wicked soul next to the painting. As soon as a player enters the room through or near the doorway, Lasso Man will come out of the painting and spawn as an actual entity. He is a variant of the Jester that almost immediately spawns in his chasing state, but he has a significantly slower roaming speed and maximum chase speed. Players must escape back through the maze while Lasso Man chases them. Since Lasso Man is a Jester variant, he will target all players in the interior until they leave and then roam the interior looking for players for the rest of the day. It is recommended to map out a specific path to escape from before entering the room and triggering Lasso Man , as running into a dead-end can easily result in death. Spray paint is especially useful for this. It is also currently possible but not advised to use extension ladders to both clip into and out of the room to get Lasso Man stuck if the door is locked, potentially even being able to avoid triggering his spawn entirely, while still obtaining the reward. plain.p-assimilated-employee: The Assimilated Employee is a hostile entity and variant of the Cadaver Bloom added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is the corpse of an employee with several tendrils coming out of their body that it uses to move around. The head of the deceased employee is also on top of and speared by one of the tendrils. Similar to the Cadaver Bloom , the Assimilated Employee will roam around until a player enters its line of sight. It will then quickly and erratically begin chasing and attempting to attack that player. It will deal 30 damage on contact and decapitate the player if they are killed by it. Since the Assimilated Employee has a whopping 28hp and will only take 1 damage from any attack, the most effective ways to deal with are to prevent its spawning entirely or trap its AI. Beyond dying through unrecoverable means or behind a locked door, players can choose to die on terrain where enemy AI does not function properly to ensure the safety of the rest of the squad. If players are in a situation where they must fight the Assimilated Employee , a shovel is most effective. It will be stunned when it gets hit and players can simply strafe backwards or in a circle and hit the Assimilated Employee every time it time it tries to rush close to them. In a desparate situation, a player can sacrifice themselves by using the Mortar Hammer to stun the Assimilated Employee for 30 seconds and open a window for another player to easily kill it. If an Assimilated Employee is killed, the body of the assimilated player will drop. This uses the same model as the Cadaver Bloom and flowers will be sprouting from the corpse. The Assimilated Employee can only spawn through the Assimilated Growth and its infection. As such, the Assimilated Employee can be encountered on Hyx . It can additionally be encountered on Faith , Filitrios , Fission-C , Gloom , and Utril if players place a mysterious object on their exteriors to spawn the Assimilated Growth on future landings. This also applies to Centrus and Vindict for placing the object on Filitrios or Utril respectively. The object is reset after being fired unless the Brooding seeds acquired from the hidden chamber on Berunah are placed onto the exteriors of Etern , Filitrios , Fission-C , Gloom , and Utril . The changes for every moon, including Faith regardless of if players moved the mysterious object in the Secret Passage , become permanent on that save file if this condition is met. Oddly, Etern does not seem to spawn an Assimilated Growth despite also having an altar. While players can be fully infected and assimilated through Hyx's hazards , the infection does not function properly if the Assimilated Growth has not spawned. plain.p-assimilated-growth: The Assimilated Growth , also referred to as its scan name Assimilation tendril , is an infectious entity that only grows within the interior of a moon. It is a variant of the Cadaver Growth added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . As the name implies, the growths are red tendrils that release foreign matter into the air to begin assimilating employees. The Assimilated Growth behaves similarly to the Cadaver Growth, selecting a random tile to initially spawn and grow on, infecting nearby players, etc. However, the Assimilated Growth can not be destroyed and has a significantly reduced base rate of infection. This is especially noticeable in singleplayer, where players can last most if not the entire day without ever dying to infection on its own without additional modifiers, such as getting hit by Hyx's hazards . When a player is about to burst and die, they will see a warning message reading "IRREGULAR ORGAN MOVEMENT DETECTED!!! FOREIGN MATTER DETECTED!!! IRREGULAR BRAIN WAVE DETECTED!!!", will hear ringing, and their screen will turn red. They will die shortly afterward and an Assimilated Employee will spawn from their body and corpse. An Assimilated Employee also spawns from infected players that die through most other means if infection has progressed far enough. An Assimilated Growth will immediately spawn in the interior of Hyx . An Assimilated Growth will also immediately spawn within the interiors of Faith , Filitrios , Fission-C , Gloom , and Utril if a mysterious object has been placed on an altar on their exteriors. An Assimilated Growth will also spawn within the interiors of Centrus and Vindict after placing the object on Filitrios or Utril respectively. The object is reset after being fired unless the Brooding seeds acquired from the hidden chamber on Berunah are placed onto the exteriors of Etern , Filitrios , Fission-C , Gloom , and Utril . The changes for every moon, including Faith regardless of if players moved the mysterious object in the Secret Passage , become permanent on that save file if this condition is met. Oddly, Etern does not seem to spawn an Assimilated Growth despite also having an altar. None of these spawns contribute to total Power Level. plain.p-asten-lab: The main entrance of Asten Lab. The Asten Lab is a lab themed interior added in the Obscurity update. It most commonly spawns on Hyx . Cafeteria - A cafeteria that is always connected to the main entrance hallway, though it can generate up a staircase connected to said hallway. Scrap can spawn here. Security Office - A security office with several monitors. This office always spawns connected to the main entrance hallway. Scrap typically spawns outside the office doors. Containment Door - A sealed door that can only be opened by completing a Secondary Objective . Other random scrap can spawn in the room behind it. Stairs - Stairs connecting to the upper or lower floor. Can often generate as dead ends. Janitor Closet - A small janitor's closet with various tools and utilities. Scrap can spawn in these closets. Lab Section - Larger rooms filled with all sorts of equipment, tables, containers, etc. Scrap can spawn in these rooms. Storage - Smaller rooms with a random assortment of things. Scrap can spawn in these rooms. Greenhouse - A corridor with several plants being grown on shelves. Office Space - A large office space with several desks, wooden walls, and padded floors. Scrap can spawn in this area. Cube - A room that connects to several hallways and has a cube structure in the middle of it. Scrap can spawn in this room. Breakable Glass - Players can break open glass containers in some Lab Section rooms by repeatedly interacting with them or by hitting them with a shovel. Scrap can spawn in these containers. Double Doors - Typically two doors instead of one will connect to the various hallways and rooms in the interior. Either door can be locked, so it's important to make sure they both are before using a key. Chemical Bomb - A small, green container that will occassionally beep. If a player gets too close to one, including through obstructions or walls, it will start beeping faster and will explode if players stick by it for too long. This explosion can deal 50 damage to or instantly kill players depending on proximity to the blast. The explosion will also leave behind a slippery green substance around the surrounding area, causing players to slide around. The Containment Door that holds the reward. One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn behind the Containment Door . Players must head to the Security Office and pull the lever located by the desk to turn on the monitors. Players can then interact with the keyboard to open and close doors as well as switch between monitors, with the monitor brightening to indicate which one the player is on. Only one door can be opened at a time and players must open the door matching the number on the Containment Door . Although players can go check what that number is first, it is often faster to brute force it by trying every door in rapid succession. If the Containment Door is successfully opened, the keyboard can no longer be interacted with and a sound effect will play. Players can then head to and open the Containment Door for their reward. Shortly after landing on a moon, five Contaminated Snare Fleas will spawn in the interior. This a variant of the Snare Flea with 1hp and a glowing green liquid on its body. All five must be killed and a sound effect will play every time one is killed. Typically, these fleas are bunched up or close by each other. If all five are killed, a sound effect will play and players can now open the Containment Door for their reward. Players must locate a small lab room containing a chemistry station, Hydrogen Peroxide, and a Sulfur Bottle. Players must insert the Sulfur Bottle into the tube above the red canister, insert the Hydrogen Peroxide into the clear container, add oxygen by interacting with the canister to the left on the ground, and turn the nozzle on the red canister to heat up the sulfur. Once complete, Sulfuric Acid will spawn as scrap for players to collect. Players must then return to the Containment Door and insert the Sulfuric Acid into the panel on the left to fry the circuits. Players can then open the door to claim their reward. If players are unsuccessful and die to the Cadaver Monstrosity , this room becomes blocked off for the rest of the day. If players are successful and kill the Cadaver Monstrosity , it will violently explode and drop a Cadaver Heart worth ▮240 to ▮351. plain.p-asteroid-13: Asteroid-13 is not a traditional moon , but an asteroid housing a "bio-weapon testing facility". The moon orbits Vow and nobody who has ever went to the moon has returned. POPULATION: Deceased/Mutated CONDITIONS: Cold, hard rocky terrain, no surface plant life detected. FAUNA: A dead ecosystem. Asteroid-13 is a a rocky environment with 7 big craters around the map and a lot of smaller ones scattered about on the moon. The buildings are domed bunkers that appear to lead underground due to the lack of any large buildings on the surface. Unlike other moons, Asteroid-13 has no sun. Asteroid-13 can experience Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, or Minefield weather by default. If Asteroid-13 is Eclipsed, the power supply will be completely broken and the lights can not be turned on. Additionally, eight enemies will spawn on the exterior and in the interior when landing. On Asteroid-13 you can hear two diffrent ambiences. One plays inside, while the other one plays outside. The player's clock is hidden while on Asteroid-13. However, time progresses at its normal speed. Asteroid-13's exterior has a power switch that lights up the entire moon to see. The power will randomly turn off sometimes, requiring a player to go back to it and turn it on again. The power will also shut off when the ship leaves the moon. This power switch is unavailable when the moon is Eclipsed, or if a player has pulled the Apparatus . Asteroid-13's interior is always foggy, similar to the vanilla Zeekerss event, which reduces visibility. Inserting the Asteroid-13 videotape found on Galetry into the projector in Galetry . Junic: Log "Geoffrey's final message" found on the exterior. Text ⁠ I am Geoffrey Samuel Smith, Agent and high commander working directly for the Emperor. This will be my final message. Until recent I have believed that my actions since the Catalyst under command of the Emperor were for some greater good. I was led to believe that all the sacrifices made were with purpose. Yet they were in vain. It wasn’t until I had lost all that I had left in my world when I realized. I now find myself here to execute one final mission. One of my own. Over the past few months we have been collecting the many experimental bioweapons that were created because of me. I made them believe we got them to study them further. Make them more dangerous. That’s what the emperor would have wanted. But I will no longer follow the wishes of that man. He sits on his golden throne while everyone else suffers by his command. I should have done something when he told me to give the order. I should have executed him right then and there. Back in the labs I smashed the glass containers for BIO-HXNV7, the deadliest weapon we have. It will hopefully kill or convert most of the people here. These loyal rats who think they’re on the winning side. There is no winning side. And I’ll make sure nobody will escape this place. Nobody will use these atrocities to further this pointless hell! plain.p-atlantean-citadel: The main entrance room in the Atlantean Citadel interior. The Atlantean Citadel is an ancient temple themed interior that frequently spawns on Atlantica , Berunah , Hyve , Junic , Roart , and Thalasso . This interior also has a rare chance to spawn on any moon. Vault - A lever can be pulled in the main entrance area to raise up a hidden Vault with symbols on it. Completing a Secondary Objective allows players to interact with the lever on it and open it. Great Hall - A large area with various branching pathways connecting to the rest of the interior that has three floors. It is always connected to the main entrance. Observatory - A room with several tower structures and a starry roof. This room is primarily for the Seek the Hidden Stars objective. Grates - A spiral staircase leading to a grate that can be pushed upward. Players can remain at the top of the staircase and jump to avoid drowning during interior floods. Sunroof - Sunlight can be seen from the roof of a large pit. This doesn't actually lead to the exterior and attempting to reach the top with a jetpack will deal 666 damage to and cut the player in half. There is a staircase players can use to avoid drowning when the interior floods. Tunnels - Tunnels that players must crouch-walk into. Entities can go into these tunnels. Chests - Chests can be found in the interior that can have scrap in them. This scrap is separate from the rest of the scrap initially generated on a moon and spawns when the chest is opened. The weather slightly alters the appearance of the interior. For example, rain can be seen pouring from the Sunroof during Rainy, Stormy, or Flooded weather. The color of this interior depends on the moon it spawns on. Axe Trap - Sometimes there can be a pressure plate that when stepped on triggers an axe to swing across, dealing 100 damage to any player caught in its path. This can be avoided by moving fast enough or jumping over the pressure plate. Eye Trap - An eye that looks around periodically. Any players that enter its line of sight will anger it, causing it to release spikes from various holes in the room dealing 33 damage. This can be avoided by avoiding its gaze or by running out of the room fast enough after angering it. A Beholder's Eye in a hidden treasure chamber. The Beholder's Eye serves as the apparatus for the interior, and two are guaranteed to spawn on either side of the interior. Both are worth ▮180, are two-handed, and weigh 36lbs. Each one is located behind a special locked door that can only be opened with a "Dungeon key", and two keys are guaranteed to spawn in the interior as scrap. When the first Beholder's Eye is taken, all other apparatus related events will be triggered and the interior will begin to flood. The player must utilize the Grates , Sunroof , remain on the third floor at the Great Hall , or simply wait outside to avoid drowning. The water level will rise and persist for about 105 seconds before draining in the next 15 seconds, making the whole sequence last for about 120 seconds. Although water can still be heard gushing in either of the Beholder's Eye rooms, the interior can only flood once a day and the second Beholder's Eye can be safely retrieved provided another key is found. The Vault that holds the reward. One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn in the Vault . If the four basins are not lit up on the Vault , players must find a room with four water basins, writing on the walls, and a door similar to the Vault door. Players must follow the instructions written on the wall to press the buttons to pour the exact amount of water needed into each basin. The numbers written use Roman numerals . If sucessful, the door similar to the Vault door will open to reveal a lever. Interacting with this lever will cause a sound effect to play and players can return to and open the Vault to get their reward. If the three fountains are not lit up on the Vault , players must find three fountains in the interior. At least one typically spawns in the Great Hall . They must then interact with five buttons in a random order to turn them on, and the buttons will reset to the starting position if pressed in the wrong order. A sound effect will play and water will begin to flow from the fountain if successful. Once all three fountains have been turned on, a sound effect will play and players can return to and open the Vault to get their reward. If the observatory looking at a star is not lit up on the Vault , players must find the Observatory . A tower light will be on and players can interact with a panel in the room to turn it up, down, left, and right. Players must locate the random position of three hidden stars. The light from the observatory will get smaller as players get closer to a star. A red star will form and a jingle will play when a star is successfully found. After players locate all three hidden stars, a sound effect will play and it will start visually storming in that room. Players can now return to and open the Vault to get their reward. Atlantean Citadel Secondary Rewards Scrap Name Image Conductive Weight (lbs) Base Value Minimum Value Minimum Solo Value Maximum Value Maximum Solo Value Ancient atlantean crown Yes 8 160 160 187 223 260 Atlantean crown Yes 8 270 270 315 377 441 Golden atlantean crown Yes 8 420 420 491 587 686 The reward is randomized, but the chance for a more valuable reward is increased by how early in the day players complete the objective and is influenced by the vanilla luck system . The value of the reward is additionally increased by a difficulty multiplier, ranging from 0.6x to 1.4x, and a solo (singleplayer) multiplier of 1.17x. Fill the Waters of Tribute is considered Easy difficulty and has a 1.0x multiplier. Turn On the Fountains and Seek the Hidden Stars are considered Hard difficulty and have a 1.4x multiplier. The base value and multipliers for objective rewards can be adjusted in the Wesleys Interior Tools config under the Secondary Objectives section. The Atlantean Tomb after starting the event. The Atlantean Tomb can randomly generate in the interior. It is a room with a center device and several inactive Eye Traps on the wall. To start the event, players must interact with three levers in a random order on the back of the central device. This will cause the door to the room to shut and the lights to turn on. Players must now interact with seven levers on the wall in a random and sequential order. Activating the wrong lever will cause all levers to reset. One strategy players can use is to give a number to each lever in their head to make it easier to remember the correct sequence. While players do this, three different traps can activate. The first trap activates immediately after starting the event, where an Eye Trap reveals itself in the center device and begins spinning towards a player. The speed of its spin depends on how far away it is from a player, and weightless players can outpace it by simply walking in the same direction of the spin. Players can not duck under its line of sight even though it looks possible to do. If it is triggered, several spikes that deal 33 damage each will come out of the center device. Players can stand on the edge of the center device to avoid the attack. After players have activated two successful levers, the Eye Traps on the wall will begin activating at random. They behave the same as the hazard and activate the spikes around them. The rate at which the Eye Traps activate and how many are active at any given time increases based on the progress made on the correct lever sequence. After players have successfully activated four levers, a giant eye will periodically become active and reveal itself on the ceiling to look down at the whole room. It will then get angry and cause several blades to shoot from the ground and slowly rotate around a ring near the center. These blades will shortly recede back into the ground and each blade does 33 damage per hit to players on contact. This attack can easily be avoided by going closer to the center. After players activate all seven levers in the correct order, all the eyes will begin to close and the center device will lower. It will then raise back up to reveal four Golden bones . Each bone is conductive, weighs 16lbs, and is worth ▮112-151. The main area of the Atlantean Citadel. Jumping to avoid drowning after interacting with a grate. Sunlight being seen from the roof. A tunnel the player can crouch into. The door leading to a Beholder's Eye. An Axe Trap after being triggered. A chest full of scrap in the Atlantean Citadel. An Eye Trap searching for trespassers. Inactive Eye Trap. The hint and room for the Fill the Waters of Tribute objective. A fountain for the Turn On the Fountains objective. The observatory light being very small, indicating a hidden star is close by. Successfully finding all three hidden stars for the objective. The giant eye appearing on the ceiling during the event.
plain.p-atlantica: Atlantica was hit by rogue rays from a supernova. This caused a disturbance in the local flow of time. Because of this, the city of Atlantica is forever doomed to sink over and over. Every inhabitant has drowned. POPULATION: Drowned. CONDITIONS: Cold wet terrain, supports aquatic plant life. FAUNA: A healthy ecosystem, fauna supports neutral behaviour. Unfinished Section This section seems unfinished. If you're a wiki editor, please help with completing this section. Primarily ocean, or coastal. split into multiple islands, bound together by small paths. Atlantica can experience Rainy, Stormy, Flooded, Foggy, Eclipsed, or Forsaken weather by default. On Atlantica you can hear an unique ambience that plays inside. The interior will flood twice a day regardless of what interior is generated. The first flood will begin at around 10:00am, flood entirely at around 11:30am, and drain at around 12:30pm. The second flood will begin at around 04:30pm, flood entirely around 06:00pm, and begin draining at around 07:00pm. It is advised to leave the interior entirely during these timeframes to avoid drowning, but it is possible to get to higher elevations in some interiors to survive. Additionally , the main entrance will begin sinking at around 04:30pm and be completely submerged at around 07:30pm. Although it is still possible to enter through the main entrance past this point in time, the only reliable way to exit through it is with a jetpack. Upon leaving the moon, you'll hear a loud burst and a light blue light will illuminate the area, followed by everything returning to how it was at the start of the day before sinking. Interacting with the map found on the exterior of Infernis . Alternatively, inserting the Atlantica videotape that randomly spawns as scrap within the interiors of Alcatras and Gratar into the projector in Galetry . Lecaro: If you go to the left of the ship and continue the path that way, you will eventually reach a fire exist that has a bridge to the right of it. Pushing down the bridge will lead to a structure that has a map that's drawn on the ground. Interacting with this will cause a short cutscene then unlock Lecaro. Gratar: Gratar videotape that randomly spawns as scrap within the interior. Text ⁠ Captain’s Log. Log 2. Location, Atlantica. After visiting Etern, we diverted course to Atlantica due to reports of ‘unnatural occurrences’ having taken place here. And I’m glad we did - most excitingly, we have discovered a map of Cosmocos on this small island not far from the mainland. We lost a crewmate trying to swim over and resorted to using jetpacks instead. And despite our loss... seeing some evidence of Cosmocos was exhilarating. It solidifies in my mind that these weren’t just delusions of mine, it was real. I was there. I saw it. I’m familiar with this terrain. I may not be able to recall with perfect clarity, but it is knowledge I possess. Or... possessed. Also of significant note - a body was discovered on Etern along with a log not dissimilar to mine. I believe we’ve obtained another piece of the puzzle, so to speak. I’ve etched it into the map. Please excuse my haste, Atlantica is sinking and I must return to the ship. Our course is set for Acidir. With one less crewmate, we should be vigilant. Cunningham, signing off. There are two pushable bridges on exterior. plain.p-backoiler-spillfish: The Backoiler Spillfish is a docile entity and variant of the Backwater Gunkfish added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is a purple stingray with two small eyes, five tentacles for its mouth, and a dark green coloration around its eyes, on its back, and on its stinger. Similar to the Backwater Gunkfish, the Backoiler Spillfish will find a location to enter its hiding state near scrap, at an AI node, or near the closest player and can be heard flopping around while it does so. If any player enters its line of sight while it moves to this location, it will immediately stop moving and enter its hiding state. After entering its hiding state, the Backoiler Spillfish will remain there indefinitely if no players are in the interior or on the exterior where it is. If players are in the interior or on the exterior where it is, it will instead check for nearby players on a timer. If this timer runs out, it will get up, leave a small puddle of oily goo behind, and find a new location to hide. If a player steps on, hits, or remains too close to a Backoiler Spillfish for too long, it will be frightened and spray all nearby players with goo that covers their hud. It will then flee, leaving behind a trail of slippery and oily goo that lasts for the rest of the day. Two universal bugs exist for the Backwater Gunkfish and all its variants. Firstly, all of them practically have 5hp instead of 4hp, as they only die after their hp drops below 0 rather than at 0. Secondly, all of them will use the same goo as whichever one first sprayed goo on a moon. For example, the Backoiler Spillfish will use the same goo as the Springwater Hotfish if the latter sprayed goo first, making the Backoiler Spillfish capable of killing players. However, these are mostly just auditory or visual differences. The Backoiler Spillfish only has a chance to spawn within the interiors of Oldred (25.97%) and Thalasso (9.80%). The Backoiler Spillfish has the same entry as the Backwater Gunkfish. Backwater Gunkfish ⁠ Backwater Gunkfish Sigurd's danger level: 0% but these little goopy goblins wont leave me ALONE Scientific name: Infectum linteum The Backwater Gunkfish is a type of Gunkfish of the family Mobulidae. Unlike the other types of Gunkfish, the Backwater Gunkfish spends most of its time on land. It can inhabit any damp, warm space where a water source is present. Its body is fat, flat, squishy and gelatinous, the width of a doormat. Its tail, slightly harder than the rest of its soft body, can range from 2-3 feet in length. When stressed, its tail is often curled up over its head to position for firing mucus or to shake and rattle as a deterrent. The Backwater Gunkfish feeds off organic material on surfaces, and for this reason, it is found most often around polluted water, swamps, or dirty sewers. When frightened, the Gunkfish can use an opening in its tail to release a burst of a thick, green mucus mixed with saliva to defend itself; the Backwater Gunkfish keeps an especially large "reserve" for emergency situations and can squirt multiple times. When needed, it uses part of this extra reserve to excrete from its body, increasing its mobility on land. The Backwater Gunkfish is harmless and is considered a natural cleaner of its preferred environments. Its mucus is a disinfectant; though it is not safe or healthy to consume, it is unlikely to cause major harm if it enters the body through the eyes or nose. Its smell is often described as a mix of vinegar and lard, and it is slightly warm when freshly excreted. Though not directly harmful, the Backwater Gunkfish is often considered a notorious pest to water treatment facilities and petroleum refineries. The gunkfish itself is evasive, capable of fitting itself into very small holes and pipes, and its mucus is arduous to remove once it has hardened, forming a substance comparable to ice. For all these reasons, the Backwater Gunkfish has lead to many accidents and should be taken seriously. Today, pest removal services are well-accustomed to safe Gunkfish removal and relocation operations, and there are many affordable options if you believe there is one in the area. The best way to prevent a Gunkfish infestation is to keep your environment clean and dry and to close off any access to standing water. Audio Action Sound Flopping Sting Spitting Goo Sliding Whining Dying While the Backoiler Spillfish uses the same flopping sound effect as the Backwater Gunkfish in-game, it does have a unique flopping sound effect with the unused vocals from the vanilla game. plain.p-backwater-cryofish: The Backwater Cryofish is a docile entity and variant of the Backwater Gunkfish added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is a light blue and white stingray with two small eyes, five tentacles for its mouth, and a grey coloration around its eyes, on its back, and on its stinger. Similar to the Backwater Gunkfish, the Backwater Cryofish will find a location to enter its hiding state near scrap, at an AI node, or near the closest player and can be heard flopping around while it does so. If any player enters its line of sight while it moves to this location, it will immediately stop moving and enter its hiding state. After entering its hiding state, the Backwater Cryofish will remain there indefinitely if no players are in the interior or on the exterior where it is. If players are in the interior or on the exterior where it is, it will instead check for nearby players on a timer. If this timer runs out, it will get up, leave a small puddle of icy goo behind, and find a new location to hide. If a player steps on, hits, or remains too close to a Backwater Cryofish for too long, it will be frightened and spray all nearby players with goo that covers their hud. It will then flee, leaving behind a trail of slippery and icy goo that lasts for the rest of the day. Two universal bugs exist for the Backwater Gunkfish and all its variants. Firstly, all of them practically have 5hp instead of 4hp, as they only die after their hp drops below 0 rather than at 0. Secondly, all of them will use the same goo as whichever one first sprayed goo on a moon. For example, the Backwater Cryofish will use the same goo as the Springwater Hotfish if the latter sprayed goo first, making the Backwater Cryofish capable of killing players. However, these are mostly just auditory or visual differences. The Backwater Cryofish has a chance to spawn on a few moons, most commonly spawning on Glace . Moon Name Interior or Exterior Spawn Chance Glace Both 14.58%, 11.59% Thalasso Interior 9.80% Polarus Interior 6.11% Extort Interior 4.63% The Backwater Cryofish has the same entry as the Backwater Gunkfish. Backwater Gunkfish ⁠ Backwater Gunkfish Sigurd's danger level: 0% but these little goopy goblins wont leave me ALONE Scientific name: Infectum linteum The Backwater Gunkfish is a type of Gunkfish of the family Mobulidae. Unlike the other types of Gunkfish, the Backwater Gunkfish spends most of its time on land. It can inhabit any damp, warm space where a water source is present. Its body is fat, flat, squishy and gelatinous, the width of a doormat. Its tail, slightly harder than the rest of its soft body, can range from 2-3 feet in length. When stressed, its tail is often curled up over its head to position for firing mucus or to shake and rattle as a deterrent. The Backwater Gunkfish feeds off organic material on surfaces, and for this reason, it is found most often around polluted water, swamps, or dirty sewers. When frightened, the Gunkfish can use an opening in its tail to release a burst of a thick, green mucus mixed with saliva to defend itself; the Backwater Gunkfish keeps an especially large "reserve" for emergency situations and can squirt multiple times. When needed, it uses part of this extra reserve to excrete from its body, increasing its mobility on land. The Backwater Gunkfish is harmless and is considered a natural cleaner of its preferred environments. Its mucus is a disinfectant; though it is not safe or healthy to consume, it is unlikely to cause major harm if it enters the body through the eyes or nose. Its smell is often described as a mix of vinegar and lard, and it is slightly warm when freshly excreted. Though not directly harmful, the Backwater Gunkfish is often considered a notorious pest to water treatment facilities and petroleum refineries. The gunkfish itself is evasive, capable of fitting itself into very small holes and pipes, and its mucus is arduous to remove once it has hardened, forming a substance comparable to ice. For all these reasons, the Backwater Gunkfish has lead to many accidents and should be taken seriously. Today, pest removal services are well-accustomed to safe Gunkfish removal and relocation operations, and there are many affordable options if you believe there is one in the area. The best way to prevent a Gunkfish infestation is to keep your environment clean and dry and to close off any access to standing water. plain.p-baduck: The Baduck is a hostile entity and variant of the Baboon Hawk added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It resembles a rubber ducky and a small Baboon Hawk as a rotund, bipedal creature with a bird-like skull, yellow skin, an orange beak, brown and orangish fur on its back, and bat-like wings. It has rows of fanged teeth inside its beak it uses to bite players. The Baduck is almost identical to the Baboon Hawk in terms of behavior and AI, spawning in groups of two, often scouting around in groups, having the same checks for when to attack a player, etc. While the Baduck does have a predetermined territory with the same three pikes as the Baboon Hawk, they will sometimes just return to wherever they had spawned with scrap and player corpses as well. The primary differences between the two are just their stats. The Baduck is easier to kill due to its reduced hp, but its tiny size can make it more annoying in general. The sheer number of Baducks that spawn can also quickly become an issue if they all decide to gang up on players at once. The Baduck has a 66.67% chance to spawn in the interior, on the exterior, and on the exterior during daytime on Duckstroid-14 , exclusively spawning on this moon. Players must type in "baboonduck" as one word to access this entry, as the terminal will attempt to redirect to the entry for the Baboon Hawk otherwise. plain.p-berunah: Endless deserts, nothing but sand. Except for the occasional temple hidden between the hills of sand. They say below the sand lies an ancient civilisation hidden from time. POPULATION: - CONDITIONS: Hot, endless deserts, ancient artifacts detected. FAUNA: Populated by very few species. Unfinished Section This section seems unfinished. If you're a wiki editor, please help with completing this section. Berunah environment Berunah can experience Stormy or Eclipsed weather by default. This moon has a default day speed multiplier of 0.75, meaning the player can stay on the moon for longer. Shortly after landing, a sandstorm will blow through. This will lower the sand in the area and reveal the ruins that make up the exterior. The following content contains spoilers for completion. Once the sandstorm has passed, a stairway will be revealed directly in front of the main entrance door. Going down this stairway will lead to an area with an interactable statue on the left side. After interacting with this statue, inserting a "Crystal cube", which is found on the exterior of Cubatres , into the hole the statue's light is shining through will reveal a hidden chamber. Inside will be five brooding seeds and a glowing eye at the end of the chamber. The player must return all these brooding seeds to the ship, but can also approach the eye for an explanation on what to do with these seeds. The player must place the brooding seeds onto altars on the exteriors of Etern , Filitrios , Fission-C , Gloom , and Utril . Doing so will alter the exteriors and interiors of these moons any time players land on those moons afterward until the player is fired. These changes become permanent on that save file once all five seeds are placed prior to being fired. Berunah's exterior will also be permanently altered on that save file once all five seeds are placed and players have entered the hidden chamber at least once. Once all five brooding seeds have been placed, the player must return to Berunah and the hidden chamber. A "Chunk of Overseer" will now be in the hidden chamber. Near the main entrance, a lever that a statue is looking at will now be interactable nearby. This will raise up the shrine of purification to insert the chunk into, and a cutscene will play shortly afterward. After the cutscene, the destiny item "Stone of purification" will spawn behind the ship. This allows the player to achieve Ending 3. Logging "My task 5" found on the exterior of Faith . End: Acquire the destiny item "Stone of purification" on the exterior after completing the moon exclusive content and insert it into the destiny item slot before taking off in the abandoned ship on Repress . plain.p-black-and-white-confetbees: The Black and White Confetbees are a hostile entity and variant of the Mask Hornets added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . As the name implies, they look like small pieces of black and white confetti. Similiar to the Mask Hornets, the Black and White Confetbees roam around the interior until finding a player to chase. They will quickly deal 10 damage per hit to players on contact. They move rather slowly, being even slower than a player at walking speed in straightaways, and can be greatly hindered by doors. A general strategy for dealing with the Black and White Confetbees during the event is to walk around the edge of the arena and group up all the bees before quickly moving to the other side of the room once it is about to spin. This helps in getting the bees closer to the center pillar to potentially get caught on it or slowed down by it once the spinning starts. Three Black and White Confetbees are spawned during the Colorless Spiral event in the Carnival . These spawns do not contribute to the total Power Level, and the Max Count and Power Level of the Black and White Confetbees only matters if players modify spawn tables to spawn the Black and White Confetbeees elsewhere. While the Black and White Confetbees do have a unique bestiary entry, they share the same terminal keyword, "confetbees", as the Confetbees and it will typically override that entry. However, there is little difference between the two entries. Confetbees ⁠ Joy and fun, yet without color

While the Council of Rule is still highly against the study and use of biological warfare, there must be a way to convince them otherwise. ..I understand that it is a very dangerous idea which.. In theory.. Could ruin more lives than I can count as well as cause a financial catastrophe within this region.. But I trust the Emperor knows this and I am sure he has a plan which I will be made aware of soon. He does not sit upon the throne without reason. After this log I might write a letter to my wife Madeline as I will be leaving 235-Calist the next morning for a meeting with the Emperor. Agent G- Signing off. - Michael's Resignation Letter from the Council: Image & Text ⁠ To start off my statement I would like everyone to remember why the use of biological warfare was made illegal in the first place. Not two hundred years ago, over in the Altra region when the study and use of biological weapons was allowed still. A conflict between two dominions turned to bloodshed. This war is now known as one of the most devastating wars in all of time across the known regions. And it was the weaponry they used which marked this war as the deadliest one in history thus far. The most commonly used was the melting gas made with the spores of an acidic super-fungi. When it touched the skin or was inhaled, it would melt the victim from the inside out. And the majority of victims were not military but civilians. Surely I do not speak for myself when I say- This musn't happen again. - Michael Dunton - an acting chairman of the council, and his experiences on Calist before the war: Image & Text ⁠ I understand that I am writing on an official document but I have overheard something I feel like I shouldn't have. However it seems important enough to have it written down for later. While I walked through the halls near the office secions. I heard a faint discussion through one of the closed doors. It was the Emperor talking to his closest agent. While I do not exactly recall what was said, I do remember them discussing the case as it stands. Their strategy is unusual. The agent seemed sceptical while the Emperor remained adamant. Understandibly so. Apparently their next argument will be that biological weapons might come in use if, say, a swarm of unidentified lifeforms from beyond the known regions invade that of ours. Not impossible but certainly not plausible. I am going to try figuring out more about the Emperor's plans. Image & Text ⁠ I followed him through the vast halls of this citadel, hoping to see if he revealed anything else. But when I turned the corner, he had vanished into one of the storage rooms. Which is particularly strange I thought. And when I put my ear up against the door. I heard him talk again. He sounded rather monotone. Having a discussion with himself. Or so I thought. It wasn't until he said 'my overseer' when I realised he was talking to someone or.. something. I hid around the corner when he left the storage closet. And he quietly mumbled 'The seed must grow' as he left the hallway. I am uncertain what any of this means but I feel something larger is a play here. Image & Text ⁠ I, Michael Dunton hereby resign from my position on the council. I feel there are things at play that are bigger than they seem. While I am certain that I would not be believed if I brought this up myself, I have left my notes and recordings in my office. I do not wish to be part of what's happening or what's to come. Strange things are going on in this council, and in this case. During the 4th and previous conference it seems to me that all sense of logistics are thrown out the window. I will take my leave on the day of the 5th and final conference. It is best to carry my words with heavy thought. -Michael Dunton When the weather is eclipsed, the sky on Calist spins significantly faster.

You can stop the engineer, but not his machine. C. Darter: You’re lost, Sol. You’re lost in your own fantasy. S. Underhill: Don’t you see it? The cities we’ve saved? The people exist in peace. Darter: You can’t call it peace when you’re the one bringing war. Maybe I can’t stop the project. But I can stop you. —----------------------- Emergency recording ended This recording can randomly spawn as scrap within the interior. Text ⁠ It strikes a fear in me, rooted deep within my ocean of thought. He kept asking about it and I don't even have the full answer. They have a way of operating that makes them invisible to not only the surface but even those who'd consider themselves high up the ladder. But I know they're here. They're everywhere. Stare long enough into the abyss, you start seeing things. Holes in reality. Fissures in logic. Yet you shake your head and pretend it was your eyes playing tricks on you. I see them. Companies appear more and more frequent like an infestation of roaches from influential businessmen to lower class entrepreneurs. All with history, documents, lives. Processed within our systems. It's usual. Standard practice. Nothing strange about it. But you look closer. You read their documents. Everything seems normal until.. you get a glimpse. A date mismatched. A name changed. Manlike mistakes, for sure. Look deeper, closer. Children without proof of birth. Deposits from companies that only registered days later. Trades between people who don't even know each other. Fissures. I've never observed them, my superiors have never seen them. Only stories.. irregularities. Seemingly random. But I think they are connected. They're here. And I believe they're scared. There is something here that scares them, threatens them. Makes them slip up. And if something is here that scares the corporate entity that’s able to twist our reality no matter where in our galaxy. You best know I sleep with one eye open. Carnate takes the longest to unlock of any moon in Wesley's Moons, requiring a minimum of routing to 15 different moons.
