plain.p-carnival: The main entrance of the Carnival. The Carnival is a circus and funhouse themed interior added in the Obscurity update. It only spawns commonly on Carnate and has a very rare chance to spawn on any moon. Tent - A yellow and red tent that the main entrance spawns in. Button Room - A room with a large container and a button that always spawns in the Tent . This is the reward room for the Secondary Objectives . Server Room - A room that can generate in the Tent with server racks and shelves. Scrap can spawn here. Funhouse - The primary area of the interior with red and white walls and wooden floors. The majority of scrap spawns around the various rooms in cabinets, on tables, etc. It is connected to the Tent through a large doorway with two eyes and the shape of a mouth. Spinning Tunnel - A catwalk leading into a tunnel that is spinning. Crystal Ball - Rooms with large crystal balls on center tables or small crystal balls and smaller tables in grated areas. These rooms can generate without a crystal ball on them and commonly have scrap. Abyss - A long wooden walkway that borders on a massive, pitch black area with practically nothing in it. The Traverse the Tightropes objective spawns here. Glass Maze - A maze of glass can spawn that leads to the Glass maze trophy , the apparatus of the interior. It weighs 21lbs and is worth ▮80. If a player takes it off its pedestal, all apparatus related events will be triggered and the glass floor beneath will start cracking. Players must quickly run off it before it breaks and they fall into the pits that act as quicksand below. Ambient music can be heard playing around the interior. Different music can also play in the Spinning Tunnel and Crystal Ball rooms. Broken Door - Some doors fall to the ground after being opened. Varying Door Sizes - Some doors are large while other doors are small and require players to crouch through them. Rotating Room - A circular room that periodically spins around, disorientating players and changing where they need to enter or leave through. Tightropes - A narrow rope can sometimes connect two areas. Boxing Glove - A boxing glove can pop out from the floor and punch through a doorway after a door is opened, dealing 100 damage to any player it hits. Depending on the direction players come from, there can be a raised area on the floor that indicates where the glove will pop up from and players can prepare to avoid it. This door will remain open for the rest of the day. Hammerbot - Small robots with glowing eyes can be found around the interior. Walking into their line of sight will cause them to beep and do an overhead slam with a comically large hammer. This hammer will deal 999 damage to all players it hits. The robot usually misses if a player is as close as possible to it due to the hammer's handle. Mouth Pit - An opening in the floor with a painting resembling an open mouth that players can fall into Death Pit - A pit with broken wood platforms for players to walk on to jump over them. Some tiles also have a black floor that gives the illusion of being a death pit while being safe. The Button Room that holds the reward and masks indicating the Traverse the Tightropes objective spawned. One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn after pressing the button in the Button Room . If the Button Room has balloons in it, players must find and pop four balloons within the interior with a shovel or knife. After popping a balloon, a sound effect will play to indicate it was popped and Confetbees will spawn. This is a variant of the Mask Hornets. Once all four balloons are popped, players can return to and press the button in the Button Room for their reward. If the Button Room has cages in it, players must find a room in the interior with similar cages and a large clown face. Approaching the nose will prompt players to press it, switching the prompt to "Run" if pressed. Music will begin playing throughout the whole interior and all players must leave the interior within the next 40 seconds. When time is up, the interior will explode and deal multiple instances of 9,999 damage to all remaining players inside. This also disables the power for the rest of the day. This explosion can be heard from the exterior and a sound effect will play afterward. Players can now press the button in the Button Room to receive their reward. If the Button Room has masks on the wall, players must make their way to the Abyss . Several wooden pillars, tightropes, and lights will now be in this area. Players must make their way through the maze to the other side and interact with a mask. A jetpack can also be used to get across. After the mask is interacted with, a sound effect will be heard and players can now return to and press the button in the Button Room for their reward. The value of the reward is additionally increased by a difficulty multiplier, ranging from 0.6x to 1.4x, and a solo (singleplayer) multiplier of 1.17x. All of Carnival's Secondary Objectives are considered Medium difficulty and have a reward multiplier of 1.15x. The base value and multipliers for objective rewards can be adjusted in the Wesleys Interior Tools config under the Secondary Objectives section. The Colorless Spiral after activation. A small black and white room with a center pillar can randomly spawn somewhere in the Funhouse . If a player enters the room and walks to the other end of it, the room will abruptly start to spin upwards and trap them inside. It will also turn the lights on and begin playing music. Once the room has spun fully upwards, Black and White Confetbees will spawn. This is a variant of the Mask Hornets that players must avoid. While moving around this room can give the illusion of it spinning, it doesn't start spinning until later when the music gets faster and the room begins to spiral downwards. A second Black and White Confetbees will spawn when the spinning stops. The room will then shortly spin back upwards and a third Black and White Confetbees will spawn after it stops. Finally, the room will quickly spiral all the way back down to the ground floor and spawn the reward. The Black and White Confetbees will be in the interior for the rest of the day. Black and White Confetbees struggle to catch up to players that are weightless and manage their stamina to sprint away in bursts, but will likely collide with players when the room spins them around violently. A general strategy to mitigate this is to move along the edge of the room and group up all the bees before quickly moving to the other side of the room past the center pillar once the room is about to spin. This helps in getting the bees closer to the center pillar to potentially get caught on it or slowed down by it once the spinning starts. Regardless of the strategy used, the event itself is rather forgiving due to the low 10 damage per hit from the bees and the bigger problem is often dealing with the bees in the interior for the rest of the day. The current reward for this event is six random scrap from the loot table below. You can help finishing this page if you trully want to. Introduction Welcome! Welcome to city 17- sorry! wrong wiki. Welcome to Characters page! A page dedicated to all characters in this mod. The formula for this page is somewhat like this: First, there are the general statistics, then, the storyline of any given character is a summary of all of the logs and other scraps of lore present IN the mod, no fanon nor answers from Wesley from outside of the mod included. Agent Geoffrey Full Name: Geoffrey Samuel Smith Occupation: High Commander and Agent of the Emperor Status: Deceased, killed either by a coil-head or infected with BIO-HXNV7 on Asteroid-13 Marital Status: Married to Madeline Smith ( also deceased, blown up with Calist ) Children: more than one (all also blown up with Calist) Age: Middle-aged Voice Actor: Audio Knight, creator of Starlancer Moons Place of birth: Unknown Place of death: 57 Asteroid-13 Disclaimer: Geoffrey's storyline is presented backwards in the game, but I have flipped it here for the sake of logic! Geoffrey's Storyline: We "first" hear of Agent Geoffrey in his first log on Calist, where he and the Council Of Rule ( aka God knows who, thanks for clarifying anything, Wesley, no, actually we know one member, Michael Dunton, more on him later. ), are 4 weeks into a debate about the usage of bio-weapons. The Council is very much against any use of the bio-weapons, and Geoffrey has been trying his best to convince them otherwise, despite knowing what atrocities can bio-weapons cause, because he is somewhat supposed to represent the Emperor after all. After finishing his first log, Geoffrey ( possibly ) writes a letter to his Wife, Madeline Smith, before leaving Calist and heading to Polarus for the final meeting with the Emperor. On Polarus, despite his best efforts to explain how the council is "very adamant about not allowing any bioweapons to be used or studied" to the Emperor, it was all in vain, as the Emperor ignored his reasoning, and instead, told Geoffrey to give the order for the Triton Military to nuke Calist. He gave the order, "in the name of the Emperor", knowing what this incident will bring about. After being assured that his family will get sent off to Trite ( Editor Zenny here, uhh, spoiler alert: They went fucking nowhere and got blown up with Calist ), he ends his log, and heads off to March, where he is tasked with assembling a team to research the moon of Cosmocos, including Captain Donahue and more notably, at the time, Lieutenant Commander Cunningham.

plain.p-confetbees: The Confetbees are a hostile entity and variant of the Mask Hornets added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . As the name implies, they look like small pieces of confetti in various colors. Similiar to the Mask Hornets, the Confetbees roam around the interior until finding a player to chase. They will quickly deal 10 damage per hit to players on contact. They move rather slowly, being even slower than a player at walking speed in straightaways, and can be greatly hindered by doors. The Confetbeees are spawned in the same location as a balloon after it is popped for Pop the Balloons objective in the Carnival . As such, a maximum of four Confetbees can be in the interior at any given time. These spawns do not contribute to the total Power Level, and the technical Max Count and Power Level of the Confetbees only matters if players modify spawn tables to spawn the Confetbees elsewhere. While the Confetbees do have a unique bestiary entry, they share the same terminal keyword, "confetbees", as the Black and White Confetbees and it will typically be redirect to that entry instead. However, there is little difference between the two entries. Confetbees ⁠ Joy and fun A balloon for the objective.
plain.p-contaminated-snare-flea: The Contaminated Snare Flea is a hostile entity and variant of the Snare Flea added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It looks identical to the Snare Flea as a large pink centipede, but it has a glowing green liquid all over its body. Like the Snare Flea, the Contaminated Snare Flea will find a random location in the interior to attach itself to the ceiling and wait for a player to walk underneath them. If a player encounters the Contaminated Snare Flea before it attaches itself to the ceiling it may abruptly change direction and find a different spot nearby. There can also be instances where part of the Contaminated Snare Flea is visible on the floor because it is on the ceiling in the room below. Whenever a player walks underneath the Contaminated Snare Flea , it will fall from the ceiling and either land on the player's head or begin chasing them to try and attach itself to their head. It slowly deals 10 damage per hit to the player it is attached to, eventually killing them. In singleplayer, the player will instead be dropped to critical hp the first time the Contaminated Snare Flea attaches to them on a moon. The Contaminated Snare Flea can be removed from a player's head and killed by using a weapon, leaving the interior, or by teleporting the player. Five Contaminated Snare Fleas will almost immediately spawn in the interior upon landing if the Containment Breach Objective is generated in Asten Lab . These five fleas generally all group up or are close by each other. These spawns do no contribute to total Power Level, and the Max Count and Power Level of the Contaminated Snare Flea only matter if players modify spawn tables to spawn the Contaminated Snare Flea elsewhere. The Contaminated Snare Flea shares the same entry as the Snare Flea. If players only scanned the Contaminated Snare Flea and wish to view the entry, they will likely need to enter "contaminatedsnareflea" as one word for the terminal to properly register and display it. Snare fleas ⁠ SNARE FLEA Sigurd's danger level: 30% Scientific name: Dolus-scolopendra. A very large arthropod of the class chilopoda. Its body produces a silk which it primarily uses to propel itself to places where it is concealed. Its exoskeleton is somewhat fragile, and they can die from long falls. The snare flea does not produce venom, nor does it have a strong bite. It makes up for this weakness with its ability to tighten itself around large prey to suffocate. The snare flea thrives in dark, warm areas. It cannot survive low temperatures and generally avoids open air and sunlight take the rats outside or just beat the hell otu of them! i think their insides could make a good milkshake,, Audio Action Sound Shrieking Hitting the Ground Walking Suffocating the Player Dying Several Contaminated Snare Fleas in one location. The only place that's not monitored here is a small storage closet near the stairs atop the upper floor. If I can sneak in there. With the right timing... I can give him what he deserves. Image & Text ⁠ This is writ with bloodied hands. Parts of Jareck's brain still between my fingernails. I succeeded. My chest is bleedin. A searing pain from one side to the other. I believe he shot me in my ambush. Though I only geel it now. My adrenaline kept me going. I was on top of him. Every fist that struck his face was fueled by unmatched anger. I asked what happened to my wife and child.. He didn't even know who I was. I now realise the road I drove would lead to nowhere. I killed the man I hated so much. Yet nothing's changed. I feel no different. My family is still missing. And soon my breath will be my last. I was damned from the day I was taken. My Task 4 is a note written by an unknown person who came to Core to get fuel to complete their "task." It can be found as scrap within the interior. Image & Text ⁠ As per usual, I leave a note. I'm only getting closer to completing my task. The cancer that grows within me makes me feel weaker by the day. But I must continue. He will heal me. I must say I enjoyed the peace that Dreck brought me. It was cold yet empty. It felt like nothing was there to bother me. I felt alone but.. the good kind. I really.. needed that. The war had quite a toll on me. Even if it's all I know. I mean. I was practically created by it. Just like many others. ... I should get the fuel I came here for and proceed to Faith. Main entrance
plain.p-corpse-crawler: The Corpse Crawler is a relatively passive entity and variant of the Spore Lizard . It is an employee's corpse stuffed with machinery, being riddled with spikes protruding out of the employee's body. It additionally has four hydraulic legs, a mechanical spine, and a pale baby head with hollowed out eyes. Similar to the Spore Lizard, the Corpse Crawler will simply wander around until noticing a player. Upon noticing a player, they will be frightened, may pulse the various spikes on their body outward to intimidate the player, and will attempt to path away from the player and break line of sight. When cornered, the Corpse Crawler will also attempt to bite players and deal 20 damage on contact. Instead of releasing spores, the Corpse Crawler will vomit out a Gore Spike when it feels threatend. This action will deal 20 damage to nearby players. This Gore Spike acts as a hazard for the rest of the day, pulsing the metal spikes lodged in the gore outward roughly every 8 seconds and dealing 20 damage to nearby players. The Corpse Crawler is injected into the Enemy Spawns (Interior) table of any moon experiencing Hallowed weather with a weight of 28, overriding the current weight if it is lower than that. The Corpse Crawler also has a chance to spawn on many moons, most commonly spawning within the interior of Demetrica . Moon Name Interior or Exterior Spawn Chance Demetrica Interior 9.96% Desolation Interior 8.13% Hyx Interior 4.39% Filitrios Interior 2.53% Oldred Interior 2.21% Extort Interior 1.85% Asteroid-13 Interior 1.80% Descent Interior 1.14% Utril Interior 1.05% Crowd Interior 1.03% Junic Interior 0.68% Release Interior 0.68% Gloom Interior 0.43% Narcotic Interior 0.37% Corpse Crawler ⁠ CORPSE CRAWLER Scientific name: Cerec-retoma The Cerec-retoma is a device made up of a hollowed rotting corpse stuffed with machinery using parts of the nervous system as internal wiring to reduce the cost of creation. The body itself seems to serve no other purpose other than to keep the components together. Hence how it has earned the name “Corpse crawler”. It walks around through the means of four hydraulic legs which use various liquids drained from the body among which are spinal fluid and blood rather than water. The extraction happens shortly after the insertion which as a side effect severs the spine and the head from the body in a very short, yet painful method. The body is riddled with spikes protruding through the flesh and skin and can be used as a defensive method against anything that seeks to attack or destroy it. These devices were likely designed and produced by the Trite Control Corporation as the first appearances were sighted on celestial bodies surrounding the fractured remains of the Triton Empire shortly after the creation of the corporation in 2249. There they acted as remotely controlled scouts being able to search and explore through the cameras hidden within the head of the device. The usage of a human body with their organs as components meant that these scouts are purposefully temporary. The rot of the corpse making it near impossible to understand what its original internals may have looked like before deactivation. Later models discovered around 2296 no longer possessed the ability of being remotely controlled but were instead fully autonomous. The corpse crawler bears a striking resemblance to the Areck-hetoma, otherwise known as the Arachnohead which was likely an inspiration for the design. plain.p-cosmic-bracken: The Cosmic Bracken , also referred to by its scan name as Bracken? , is a hostile entity and variant of the Bracken added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . While its body structure is identical to the Bracken, it has blue leaves on its back, purple skin, and several white dots on its body. These white dots make the Cosmic Bracken's skin resemble a starry night sky, especially in the dark. Similar to the Bracken, the Cosmic Bracken will silently stalk players and attempt to sneak up behind them to snap their neck with its hands. If a player spots the Cosmic Bracken within the middle of their screen, it will be startled, begin to move towards its chosen room, wait, and repeat the whole process. Staring at the Cosmic Bracken increases the likelihood of it attempting to chase and attack the closest employee, and directly attacking the Cosmic Bracken instantly triggers this. Any player that comes into contact with the Cosmic Bracken will be killed and it will attempt to drag their corpse to its chosen room. While the Cosmic Bracken only has a a Max Count of 1, it is only found on moons where it can spawn in every table and so players can encounter up to two on the exterior. On the exterior of Glimmer , the Cosmic Bracken moving through some of the flora will make it glow and release lights resembling fireflies just like it does when a player moves through it. While this is just a visual feature, it does make it easier to tell when a Cosmic Bracken may be sneaking up on a player. The Cosmic Bracken has a 25.21%, 98.08%, and a 94.72% chance to spawn in the interior, on the exterior, and on the exterior during daytime respectively on Cosmocos . The Cosmic Bracken additionally has a 23.56%, 91.07%, and 75.32% chance to spawn in the interior, on the exterior, and on the exterior during daytime respectively on Glimmer . The Cosmic Bracken shares the same entry as the Bracken. If players have only scanned the Cosmic Bracken and wish to view the entry, they may need to type out "cosmicbracken" as one word into the terminal to avoid having the terminal try to route them to Cosmocos . Bracken ⁠ Bracken -- AKA flower man! it was flower man, you can't say othrwise! i wanted to find his body .You were the cowards Scientific name: Rapax-folium There is debate on the genus to which the Bracken belongs. It is a bipedal vertebrate with skin the color and texture of a red beat. The name was coined for what appear to be leaves protruding from its upper spine. The purpose of these is believed to be for intimidation, however not much is known about the specifics of bracken behaviour due to its illusiveness and low population. We know a little from accounts by wildlife experts who have encountered it. is a lone hunter with high intelligence. Its behavior can seem aloof; it exhibits high aggression even when unprovoked, yet it quickly backs off when confronted. However, brackens are known to up their hostility when cornered or simply watched for a long time. For this reason it's recommended to keep an eye on it but not to stare it down. No specimens have been collected dead or alive. It's theorized that upon death their bodies undergo a rapid decomposition process which is unique from other large animals. plain.p-cosmocos: Cosmocos is the long lost moon. Home to one of the Vault Key Apparati and to the Celestial Brain. POPULATION: ??? CONDITIONS: ??? FAUNA: ??? UNKNOWN ANOMALY DETECTED Unfinished Section This section seems unfinished. If you're a wiki editor, please help with completing this section. Cosmocos is dark and hard to traverse. The map changes throughout the day, as walls that were once present disappear later. There are plants that emit blue light to help guide you to the main entrance or fire exits. Cosmocos can experience Foggy or Eclipsed weather by default. If Cosmocos is Eclipsed, additional Watchers will spawn on the exterior. On Cosmocos you can hear two diffrent ambiences. One plays outside while the other one plays inside. The player's clock is hidden while on Cosmocos. However, time still progresses and Cosmocos has a day speed multiplier of 0.5, meaning the player can stay on the moon for significantly longer. Cosmocos features unique map hazards called "Watchers". They look around the area they are facing toward and will deal minor damage to the player caught in their gaze. Cosmocos has a lone interior fire exit that leads to an exterior area filled with Watchers , where the Celestial Brain and Cosmic Apparatus can be found . It is not possible to use a jetpack to reach or escape this area, as it is not part of the rest of the exterior and is surrounded by invisible walls. Removing this apparatus will anger all Watchers and cause them to look around faster. Additionally , removing this apparatus will still trigger all apparatus related events, such as the flamethrowers in the Greenhouse or the falling ceiling and locked exit doors in the Grand Armory . Logging "Cunningham's travel log 4" found on the exterior of Polarus . Alternatively, logging "Recovered secret log" that spawns as random scrap within the interior of Asteroid-13 . Glimmer: Log "Donnahue's note" found on the exterior. Gratar: Gratar videotape that spawns randomly as scrap within the interior. Alternatively, log "Cunningham's visit" that spawns as random scrap within the interior. Hyx: Acquiring the Cosmic Apparatus found via a lone fire exit within the interior and inserting into its respective slot in the hidden area in Galetry . This also requires the Royal Apparatus from Calist and the Bloody Apparatus from Demetrica . Utril: Utril videotape that spawns randomly as scrap within the interior. Text ⁠ At the behest of Captain Donahue, I am to record my own personal experiences here on Cosmocos. I was first to stumble upon this strange extraterrestrial lifeform. It seemed to be, upon first glance, perhaps a plant, or something akin to coral - something like Diploria. But when I placed my hand upon it, even through my suit, I felt - I felt as if incredible knowledge was poured into me. Knowledge of things vastly unfamiliar and unbelievably alien to me - but also of things familiar, things around me that others had been educated on, but I’d never had the opportunity to learn. It was incredible, exhilarating. Unlike anything I’ve ever experienced. But the most exhilarating thing of all was this unusual connection I feel that I’ve fostered with this thing. This being. In a sense, it felt... like a person, is perhaps the best way to put it, in terms we are capable of understanding. Like Cosmocos isn’t just a moon. Like it’s... a huge, alien life-form, sitting here in space with its own incredible ecosystem. Bizarre as it may be, I can say with confidence that I could feel what seemed to be a rush of emotions from Cosmocos itself. I still feel it now, in truth. Which sounds like insanity, doesn’t it? But it was beautiful. Like a rush of warmth, kindness, generosity. I really feel like Cosmocos wants to teach us things. Like it wants to help us grow and nurture us. The Captain has commanded that no one is to interact with this celestial brain aside from himself for our own safety. I do feel slightly disheartened by this, as I was hoping to commune with it again. I have so much more to say. It’ll be difficult to record all of this knowledge I’ve been gifted with in a comprehensible format on these recorders, but I’ll do my best over the next few cycles. Lieutenant Commander Cunningham, signing off. Text ⁠ There has been a terrible turn of events. The whole crew is celebrating, currently, after the Captain has confirmed my mad ramblings to be based in truth. That Cosmocos possesses incredible alien knowledge, and is willing to share it with us. Granted - initially, I was not entirely coherent when I tried to convey my experience with the celestial brain, but...tch, I’ll hold my tongue. He’s ordered to remove the brain and prepare for it to be taken back with us to 61-March. But this will kill Cosmocos, I know this for certain. Slowly, over time, atrophied, until it is a husk. I don’t know why the Captain, having been offered the same kindness from Cosmocos, would even consider doing something like this. It’s not right. Perhaps he doesn’t know? Perhaps we were not offered the same thing? Perhaps he knows...and he doesn’t care? He’s not a man known for his kindness, after all. I asked that we put it to a vote. Not a single person sided with me. I don’t know what to do. I don’t know what I could possibly do to dissuade the Captain that wouldn’t have me thrown in a pod set on course for a jail cell back on 61. But I have to do something. This isn’t what Cosmocos wants. And I refuse to see it die like this. Lieutenant Commander Cunningham, signing off. Text ⁠ He threatened me! That- that- heartless- I don’t know why I ever felt compelled to try and convince that man of anything, knowing he is capable of such evil. He is not a man reasoned with. Cosmocos has the most beautiful terrain I’ve ever laid eyes upon. Such gorgeous, diverse plant life. A heart. I really feel as though it has what the more spritual of us would call a soul. And the Captain has a gall to suggest that Cosmocos has tricked me, somehow. Perhaps these feelings are not my own. Perhaps these are feelings Cosmocos has imposed upon me. Regardless of whether these emotions are pre-disposed or not - with everyone ounce of my being, I feel certain that Cosmocos is a thinking, feeling moon. Isn’t that incredible? Shouldn’t that be protected? I’m going to be the one to protect it, if no one else will. Whatever the cost. If I fail, at worst, they’ll send me back to March for proper proceedings. My knowledge is too valuable. And then I’ll make it my mission to come back. If they succeed in doing this to Cosmocos... I’ll see it done that it is made whole again. Cunningham, signing off. Text ⁠ Long time no see, old friend. You gave me a real run-around, didn’t you? Going off the radar like that. You teleported yourself... nearly eight-hundred-million miles away. I didn’t even know you could do that. You are full of wonders. You didn’t want to hurt them, did you, friend? You did everything you could not to kill them. You wanted so dearly to see them learn, and grow, and help each other... I feel it. I know, I know... They’re still out there, though, aren’t they? That’s them? Lurking in the shadows. They’re protecting you now. I want to protect you too, if you’ll let me. No one will ever hurt you again. Not while I’m around. Image & Text ⁠ Day 79 Our team has gone mad. Ever since the flash, our technology seems to be malfunctioning. It is unlikely that we’ll be able to leave anytime soon. Day 80 A few on the team say they are experiencing disorientation and dizziness. Unsure as to why but it appears to be a common factor. I wonder if we’ve been hit with a large surge of radiation. We best figure out what’s wrong with the equipment so we can do a proper evaluation. Day 81 Three of us stumbled into the forest, they said, “the forest is calling to us”. If it weren’t for the fact that we need all hands on deck I would let them get lost. I’ve sent two more of us out to go and look for them. Day 82 Nobody turned up, not the three who went missing nor the ones I sent out to find them. Fantastic. Now I am starting to sense it too. Slightly disoriented and there’s this strange feel to my skin. I’ve told the rest of the team to keep working on getting the equipment fixed up. I’m heading out to the third facility. It’s not too distant. About 12000 meters north-east from here. Perhaps they have answers there. Day 83 My skin feels strange. My back hurts. It feels like something’s crawling under my shoulderblades. The path seems different from what we mapped out. I dare say I am lost. Running out of ink too. Day 84 Everything hurts. My legs below my knees are shrinking. It’s getting hard to walk. My skin has turned purple and thick. There’s something sticking out my back. Something cursed me, something cursed all of us. I don’t believe I’ll be here for much longer. There’s something very wrong here. I think I’ll just sit by this tree. I’ll write more tomorrow. Image & Text ⁠ We found the... anomalous object. It was quite far from the primary facility so we decided to construct a tunel direclty to it. There’s a lot of plants and growth in the way, it will likely take quite a bit. But when that’s finished we finally be able to further study this... thing. It’s going to take some heavy machinery so we might just bring one of our special apparatuses. plain.p-creaker: The Creaker is a hostile entity and variant of the Nutcracker added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It resembles an older and worn down Nutcracker holding a blue shotgun and has a small orange eye surrounded by a membrane. The Creaker behaves identical to the Nutcracker, having the same patrolling state, scanning state, attacking state, etc. The most notable differences are the sound effects played and the scrap dropped, being the Spooky shotgun and up to two Spooky ammo . These are functionally identical to the Shotgun and Ammo respectively, and the latter works for reloading any shotgun, but killing a Creaker is the only legitimate way to obtain either scrap. The Creaker is injected into the Enemy Spawns (Interior) table with a weight of 9 on any moon experiencing Hallowed weather. This makes the Creaker a fairly rare entity to encounter, as it can not spawn anywhere else naturally. plain.p-crowd: Crowd was one of the many moons housing mass livingspaces for the ever expanding population. This particular one was abandoned fairly early into the grand war. Ownership was transferred to the Trite Control Corporation. POPULATION: Abandoned CONDITIONS: Warm. Mildly foggy. Slightly sparse oxygen due to previous inhabitation. Crowd can experience Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Flooded, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, Hurricane, or Minefield weather by default. When Crowd experiences Flooded weather, the insides of the houses on the exterior will be filled with water immediately upon landing. The rest of the exterior will flood as normal. This moon features a trial that generates with the Spooky Manor interior. Completing it rewards the player with scrap worth a total of at least ▮400. To complete this trial: Find three radios within the interior and interact with them to switch their channel. Find the pool room with an employee in it within the interior, interact with the red button in this room, and grab the gas canister revealed underneath the red button shortly afterward. Find the garage within the interior and use the gasoline to fuel the generator next to the car. Return to the pool room, interact with the red button again, and wait for the employee to die. The reward spawns below the dead employee. If players decided to overload and blow up ResearcherxB , debris from the ship can fall onto Crowd's exterior. If players land on Crowd in the future on that save file, a mild outbreak of white mold will be present on the exterior and Infected Bunker Spiders will spawn at the start of the day. plain.p-cubatres: Cubatres is one with strange shapes and even stranger occurrences. Volatile materials are scattered across the landscapes and gathered to create the most outlandish machines. One of which being the renowned apparatus. POPULATION: Vanished. CONDITIONS: Cold, Rocky Terrain, highly volatile crystals present. FAUNA: A destroyed ecosystem. One plays inside while the other one plays outside. The highly volatile crystals mentioned are map hazards called "Cube" found on the exterior and within the interior. Any player within the energy pulse will rapidly take 10 damage per hit . Additionally , the scrap "Crystal cube" can be found on the exterior . From the front of the ship, wrap around the left wall until reaching one of the cubes. Then, hug the right wall until reaching various petrified entities surrounding the scrap. This is also the location of one of the fire exits. This scrap is required to access the hidden chamber on the exterior of Berunah . Interacting with the map found on the exterior of Utril . This moon does not unlock any other moons. plain.p-decrepit-store: The main entrance of the Decrepit Store. The Decrepit Store , also referred to as Store, is a custom interior. It only spawns on Facto, a.k.a., the Crocs inspired Lethal Company experience, by default, which is a moon that must be downloaded separately from the rest of "Wesley's Moons". After "Obscurity" update came out, this interior was removed from "Wesley's Interiors". Now you can only download its standalone version on ThunderStore . Secured Area - Rooms with many wooden crates stacked on top of each other that generate behind security doors. The majority of scrap is condensed to spawning in these rooms. Display Rooms - Rooms with a white tiled floor and many display pedestals. Scrap can generate on these pedestals. Old Storage Area - A large part of the interior will generate as a far more run-down area with a wooden tile, various stacked crates, boxes, and miscellaneous items, and more worn down mannequins. The apparatus room tends to generate in this area. Apparatus Room - Similar to the storage areas, this is a room with several stacked wooden crates. Several mannequins are lined up in front of the boxes on either side and surrounding the apparatus. Mannequins - When the apparatus is pulled, one mannequin in the interior will activate and spawn one of three unique entities: Mannequin, Broken Mannequin, or Headless Mannequin. All three are a silent variant of the Coil-Head. One of the storage areas behind a security door. One of the display rooms. Another display room. Part of the old storage area. A giant clog on display. An entrance to an apparatus area. The mannequins moving after the apparatus has been pulled. An active Broken Mannequin.
plain.p-deep-sewers: The main entrance of the Deep Sewers. The Deep Sewers is a sewers themed interior that most commonly spawns on Narcotic . This interior can be claustrophobic and maze-like due to its long, narrow hallways and corridors that connect to each other. Brick Maze - Corridors with sludge and waste that make up a large portion of the sewers. Scrap can generate in the areas with light and platforms, including the main entrance. Valve Gate - A large valve connected to a gate that typically spawns close to the main entrance and always in part of the Brick Maze . Players can open this gate after completing a Secondary Objective . Concrete Brick Maze - The other large portion of the sewers that frequently connects to loot rooms. Large Tunnel - A large tunnel with various branching pathways that can connect to various parts of the interior. Storage - A small room that generates with various objects, such as buttons on the right wall, shelving units, tools hanging on the left wall, etc. Scrap often spawns in these rooms. Locker Storage - A room with a set of lockers that has a door leading into another room partially submerged in waste. Scrap often spawns in these lockers or in the partially submerged room. Roof Grate - A small room with a sewer grate in the middle of the roof. The Snatcher can be heard and encountered here and scrap can occasionally generate here. Long Pipe - An absurdly long pipe can generate that often connects to another part of the interior. Graffiti - Graffiti can be found on various walls in the sewers. Most of it is flavor text, but some of the graffiti hints at the existence of the Treasure Room and the Snatcher . Snatcher - The Snatcher is a large creature that appears to be made up of waste with multiple eyes and limbs. The player can encounter it or its arms dangling through sewer grates at various points in the interior, but all of these encounters are auditory or visual. The liquid present in the sewers depends on the moon the interior spawns on. Snatcher (Entity) - At 05:00pm, there is a 50% chance for the Snatcher to spawn within the interior. It will roar and be heard by any players in the interior if it spawns. It is a variant of the Thumper with 8hp. The treasure room at the bottom of the staircase. The treasure room serves as the apparatus room for the interior and is its most prominent feature, although it does not have a guaranteed chance to spawn. It is a large room with many wooden platforms stacked to the left, where scrap can spawn, and a guaranteed key spawn and interactable wheel to the right. It also has a staircase submerged in toxic waste that rapidly deals 2 damage per hit to the player or 18 damage per hit to the player if they are near the bottom. At the bottom of the staircase there is a door, which can be locked, that opens to a room with many gold bars alongside cash registers, golden cups, pill bottles, and wedding rings. Other scrap can spawn in this room, though it is unlikely. Turning the wheel temporarily begins to drain the toxic waste and allows for safe travel to the bottom, taking about 12 seconds from turning the wheel to fully drain. After about another 45 seconds, the sound of rushing water will be heard and the waste will begin to rise again. Once the waste has returned to its original position, the lights will begin flickering and the power will go out with a radiation warning shortly afterward. If a player simply runs straight down and up the stairs with no strategy, tools, or additional modifications, it is possible retrieve up to three pill bottles and one cash register/gold bar while taking a little damage from the rising waste. Alternatively, the player can safely retrieve four cups/rings. This totals to an average of ▮204-264 depending on what scrap is taken. Dropping off the staircase railings can be used as shortcuts to save a tremendous amount of time during the descent. When looking at the wheel, turn around and run towards the wall and railing, jump onto the railing, and fall onto the first outer railing below. From here, look at and push up against the wall, walk or jump off to the right while remaining as close to the railing as possible, and immediately begin moving left to land onto the second outer railing. This can be repeated to reach the third outer railing, or the player can fall straight from the first to the third outer railing, and places the player at the staircase leading to the door. The second and third falls are risky, however, as missing will usually result in death. This increases the total average to ▮268-368 depending on what scrap the player grabs and what risks they're willing to take, with the most feasible maximum being two pill bottles and two gold bars. The player can also continuously drop and pick up a cash register while moving backwards to increase speed and decrease stamina usage overall. If executed correctly with the above shortcuts, a player can sacrifice most of their hp to retrieve two rings/cups, a gold bar, and a cash register for an average of ▮402. Since this requires an immense out of effort with little room for error, it is generally recommended to stick to safer and more consistent options. Although a TZP-inhalant can be useful, it usually isn't worth the price as it can not be reused. An extension ladder usually gets stuck, but can create a platform to jump to the third outer railing with less risk. A jetpack can be used to safely make two trips for six gold bars, totaling to an average of ▮936, but can be cumbersome or risky to carry into the interior and it will likely take a bit of practice for players unfamiliar with using one. The Valve Gate that has the reward room behind it. One of three unique objectives will randomly generate for players to complete for one of three valuable rewards that will spawn in the room behind the Valve Gate . If the graffiti on the wall by the Valve Gate mentions flow machines, players must find three flow machines in the interior. Players must repeatedly interact with the yellow valve and then push or pull the left and right levers to the respective left and right number position. The bottom lever position is 0 and the top lever position is 10. The lever moves up or down by 1 with each interaction. A sound effect will play after a flow machine is successfully fixed. Once all three flow machines have been turned on, a sound effect will play and players can return to and open the Valve Gate to enter the room and get their reward. If the graffiti on the wall next to the Valve Gate mentions the power box exploding, players must find two power boxes with several knobs in the interior. Players must turn each knob to the correct position indicated by a unique click sound when a player turns it to that position. These power boxes also have a written warning that faulty knobs, indicated by sparks coming out of the knob when turning it, must always be pointed upward. Trying to activate the power by pressing the red button and having a knob in an incorrect position will cause players to take 40 damage. Once both power boxes are turned back on, a sound effect will play and players can return to and open the Valve Gate to enter the room and get their reward. If the graffiti on the wall next to the Valve Gate mentions a sludge tunnel, players must go to the sludge tunnel in the Concrete Brick Maze with a yellow pipe leading to it. Inside will be an underwater maze and they must interact with several yellow valves to open the full path to a bigger valve at the end of the yellow pipe. The lights lead the way to the valves or the gates that valves open. Players must also return to the entrance of the Sludge Tunnel to avoid drowning with each trip. Once the last valve has been interacted with, a sound effect will play and players can return to and open the Valve Gate to enter the room and get their reward. The value of the reward is additionally increased by a difficulty multiplier, ranging from 0.6x to 1.4x, and a solo (singleplayer) multiplier of 1.17x. Traverse the Sludge Tunnel is considered Easy difficulty and has a 1.0x multiplier. Fix the Flow Machines and Restart the Power are considered Hard difficulty and have a 1.4x multiplier. The base value and multipliers for objective rewards can be adjusted in the Wesleys Interior Tools config under the Secondary Objectives section. An angled view of the Deep Maintenance Elevator. The Deep Maintenance Elevator can randomly generate in the interior. It is a small, rectangular platform suspended above sewage. As soon as a player stands on the elevator, both the sewage below it and the elevator itself will begin to descend. The Snatcher will appear and spray sewage onto the platform, causing it to become slippery. The Snatcher will then attempt to either hit players on the edges of the elevator, dealing 50 damage on contact, or attempt to knock players off the elevator by spitting streams of sludge at them that pushes them backwards. If players do fall off the elevator, they will likely die to fall damage or drown. Players should try to make their movements small and precise to avoid gaining too much speed and sliding around uncontrollably. If the Snatcher is going to hit players with its spit, they can position themselves to get pushed into the columns or objects at the corners of the arena. A jetpack completely trivializes this event, as players can just activate their jetpack if they begin to fall off the elevator. An extension ladder can be used to some degree as well, but is often too finnicky to be of much use. Eventually, the elevator will descend to a slightly open pipe and the Snatcher will disappear. Inside this pipe will be the Snatcher skullplate , which is the reward for the event. It is conductive, is two-handed, weighs 13lbs, and is worth ▮192 to ▮227. plain.p-demetrica: The Domes of Demetrica are places of safe harbour where one can wait out the war. Near the edge of the region, far away from conflict they promise to keep the population secure. Billions of people went. You will find them inside. POPULATION: Living happily. CONDITIONS: Warm, lush terrain, very diverse oceanic flora. FAUNA: A healthy ecosystem. Demetrica environment Demetrica can experience Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, or Forsaken weather by default. Demetrica has a unique Bloody Apparatus that spawns on the exterior. It is in a room that is directly behind the ship when the door opens and it is on top of a platform that requires a jetpack, extension ladder, or the company cruiser (not recommended) to reach. Removing this apparatus triggers all apparatus related events . Entering this room will trap the player inside and activate two walls with skulls on them . These walls move around the room in straight lines counter-clockwise and briefly stop to turn corners. To escape, there is a door on the other side of the room that has a panel to the right with multiple switches. Flicking a switch will also flick every adjacent switch and players must turn on all the switches, indicated by the switch being down and lit green, to open the door. The walls remain active for the rest of the day . If a player escapes the room through the door, both sides of the room will open and the room will be accessible for the rest of the day. If no player escapes the room through the door after triggering the trap, it will remain inaccessible for the rest of the day. Logging "Radio Message 4" found on the exterior of Filitrios . Hyx: Acquire the Bloody Apparatus on the exterior of this moon and insert into its respective slot in the hidden area in Galetry . This also requires the Royal Apparatus from Calist and the Cosmic Apparatus from Cosmocos . Alcatras: Log "Secret files" that randomly spawns as scrap within the interior. It is able to remember certain growing patern from a genetic blueprint. Meaning it's alive! But seamingly not in the traditional way we precieve living things. Our entire understanding of life was just flipped upside down. It is even able to grow these weird.. bulbs resembling eyes. It is unsure if these eyes serve a purpose.. Well.. They must.. Otherwise it wouldn't be growing them. We will refer to this as.. Cosmic Growth from now on. That's all I can say for now. Professor Harrington, over and out. Text ⁠ These old voice recorders are the worst.. Right.. We've got word from captain Donahue over at the primary facility. They have found.. something.. It appears to be something new, something unexplored. They think it might be some sort of plant which sounds exciting. Here however we've made steady progress. As mentioned before, this cosmic growth is able to grow.. eyes wherever it pleases. At first we thought it might be some sort of defense mechanism. But there's no active predators on Cosmocos from the data we've gathered. But then we noticed something strange.. One of the eyes growing in our incubators was able to move and look around, illuminating whatever it looked at. This place is full of surprises. More information soon. Professor Harrington, over and out. Text ⁠ It's been a strange past few weeks, we've heard that luitenant commander Cunningham was send back to 61 after going mad. I have no idea what that's all about. But they've started extracting this.. plant I think it was? Anyways. Research has been going steady, these illuminating eyes don't seem to have a purpose.. well.. not a definitive one at least. Ever since the Cunningham incident it appears to be more.. agressive almost. It's certainly strange. I wonder if the- *Rumbling* What is happening? Everything is bright outside?? *More rumbling* Woah. What's happening. *Agressive rumbling* There's a what coming at us?! *The sounds of a moon ripping itself apart.* We have been hit. Worse. We have been separated from Cosmocos. I.. I need to go.. Despite being in the Enemy Spawns (Interior) table, Lasso can not spawn without commands or additional modification. Wesley has previously stated Lasso was added to the table because it was funny, but Wesley also created a Jester variant called Lasso Man and potentially added it to the table in the Obscurity update. plain.p-dirty-disturbed-masked: The Dirty Disturbed Masked is a hostile entity and variant of the Masked added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is an employee with a Dirty disturbed mask attached to their face. Identical to a regular Masked, the Dirty Disturbed Masked will roam around in search of players. It looks similar to a normal player on the radar but will often be seen spinning around. It will look around, sprint, and stop sprinting randomly. If no player is within the interior, it will try to reach the main entrance and exit onto the exterior and vice versa. It will also make its way to the ship after some time to hide and wait for players to return to ambush them. If a Dirty Disturbed Masked spots a player, it will pause before beginning to chase them. If a player comes into contact with it, they'll be grabbed and the Dirty Disturbed Masked will try to convert them. This can be interrupted if the Dirty Disturbed Masked is hit. Otherwise, the player will die, their body and any scrap they were holding can not be recovered, and a second Dirty Disturbed Masked will spawn. An initial Dirty Disturbed Masked will only be spawned if a player wears and randomly gets possessed by the Dirty disturbed scrap that is a potential Secondary Objective Reward from the Toy Store . The moon now called Dormant is a desolate wasteland after having taken its part in the Grand War. While a majority has been fully destroyed, flukes in the heavy weaponry have spared this place from total destruction. A large amount of MK2 Core Heaters were used to wipe the moon off the maps. A similar, older model from those used to cause the Silent Flash. Due to the failure in technology, many of these bombs either detonated in orbit or lodged themselves firmly into the ground without detonating at all. Yet due to their unstable nature could not be retrieved. They now lie there, dormant. POPULATION: Abandoned. CONDITIONS: Warm, dry, toxic terrain, highly irradiated flora. FAUNA: An irradiated, dying ecosystem. Critical level explosive device detected. Dormant is an arid, dry, and rocky moon. While the trees and most other flora are dead, signs of life can still be found in small patches of greenery on more sandy areas. Ponds of green, toxic waste can also be found around the moon. Its most prominent landmarker is the dormant, colossal explosive behind the ship lodged into the ground. Three concrete buildings and structures as well as metal fencing can be found around the moon as well. The larger building behind and west of the ship is the main entrance and the other two structures found northwest and east of the ship are both fire exits. Dormant supports Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Forsaken, and Hurricane weather by default. Dormant naturally generates mines on its exterior, which can deal 30 damage to players or instantly kill nearby players and most entities depending on proximity to the blast. If any player causes a mine to detonate, it will destabilize the Unstable core-heater , i.e., the bomb. If five mines are detonated, the bomb will explode and instantly kill all players. A Floppy disc machine can be found on the other side of this area. It is recommended to bring tools like a Jetpack or TZP-Inhalant to make crossing the area less risky. Players can not access this area from the exterior normally, as there is a damage trigger on the roof of the area that deals 999 damage to players that pass through it. My job was simple but it payed well. Now I find myself in this shithole.. Doomed to work until my back snaps in two. Doomed to never see my wife and child ever again. We lost good men but we took control over the facility. In the control room I gained access to the ships which we are now loading up to make our escape. It appears as though the guards called in an emergency. I expect more of them to come soon. I'll shoot a couple pipes on my way out in hopes that some of them suffocate in the leaking gas. But more importantly. I went searching. And I found. Jareck Hill was here 6 days ago. The log I read indicates that he now finds himself in another facility. The flight route was set to 842 Core. plain.p-droop: The Droop is a hostile entity and a variant of the Barber added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is a tall, slender, and humanoid looking creature with pitch black skin. It has two glowing white eyes and a wide open mouth that emits a light below it. It will shrink itself down to fit into tighter spaces, such as moving around in the interior. Unlike the Barber, the Droop is always visible. The Droop also does not increase or does not increase at a noticeable speed as time progresses. Otherwise, the Droop behaves similarly to the Barber, making an audible buildup noise before stepping (teleporting) to a random location within a set distance. If a player enters its line of sight, it will attempt to move towards them. Any player that walks in-between the hands of a Droop will be temporarily blinded and take 100 damage. This is an important distinction from the Barber's instant kill, as it allows players to survive a hit from the Droop by overcapping their health with a Health-stim . The Droop has a 51.95% chance to spawn in the interior and a 91.67% chance to spawn on the exterior of Xenphir , exclusively spawning on this moon. Droop ⁠ DROOP Sigurd's danger level: uhhhh I dnot know but thsi sou nds horrifyign Scientific name: Vorictus-detoma The Vorictus-detoma, garnered the name “Droop” due to its drooping appearance. Its arms, legs and neck are exceptionally long, likely due to the body deformation which happens in the process of a Droop’s creation. The Droop is not officially classified as a non-human creature, while it no longer possesses the humanity it once did, it technically is still human. Only with the effects of prolonged exposure to V-Radiation. V-Radiation is an incredibly rare phenomenon and has previously had very adverse and unexplainable effects on creatures and places, often leading to deformation and destruction. Sightings of V-Radiation were extremely rare up until the Grand war where it was occasionally used to cause mass destruction. However, even by supporters of the use of biological warfare, it was greatly frowned upon due to its cruel and otherworldly effects often rendering places uninhabitable. While there have not been many encounters, the majority of the Droop were likely everyday civilians affected during the war. Direct exposure to gamma or beta rays of V-Radiation vaporises the average unprotected human, leaving behind what can only be described as a shadow or a memory where they once were. It is not certain what exactly it is that they leave behind but it is thought to no longer be alive. However there have been rumors of these shadows stalking or moving in the dark. When exposed to alpha rays of V-Radiation you won’t immediately notice any harmful effects aside from a slight headache or brief dizziness. But from the moment of exposure you have been infected with a unique type of radiation sickness. While it doesn’t break your DNA, it does change it which only becomes noticeable after a few days. Skin might start feeling heavy and organs might move around during a very painful process. If the infected is still alive 13 days past the first exposure, changes start happening to the brain, often noting highly irregular brainwaves. From this point onwards it is only a husk of its former self. While it is on a technical level not death, this is what we consider the moment of death. The person is unrecoverable and the body is deformed to an unrecognisable level where the skin and muscles resemble a droopy obsidian. There has not been any research from this point onwards. plain.p-duck: The Duck is a hostile entity and variant of the Red Pill , an unused vanilla entity, added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is literally just a large a rubber ducky. The Duck always knows where players are and will attempt to move towards the closest player regardless of location. For example, if a player is in the interior and the Duck is on the exterior, it will still attempt to path as close as it can to the player in the interior. This makes the Duck behave similarly to a permanently active Jester, but its movement is similar to that of a Thumper, rapidly accelerating while moving and having to slow down to make turns. The Duck is technically killable and stunnable, but lacks an actual hitbox and is completely invulnerable in-game. Likewise the Duck technically has a Door Speed Multiplier of 1, but is incapable of opening doors in-game. Any player that comes into contact with the middle of the Duck will violently explode into chunks and their body can not be recovered. The Duck has a 33.33% chance to spawn in the interior, on the exterior, and on the exterior during daytime on Duckstroid-14 , exclusively spawning on this moon. The Duck stuck on a door. Dune is a large moon mainly consistent of expansive stretches of desert with a few oceans in between. It used to be a popular place for lavish mansions and buildings for those who could afford such luxuries. However due to frequent incidents with Earth leviathans, cacti infestations and large sandstorms, most of these locations have been left abandoned. POPULATION: Abandoned. CONDITIONS: Hot, dry terrain, large deserts. FAUNA: A simple ecosystem, dominated by earth leviathans. Dune is largely a dry and somewhat hilly desert. Most of its flora is cacti and bushes, and a small oasis can be found to the right and south of the ship. There is a ravine in front of and to the left of the ship with two bridges to cross over it to a large building, which is the main entrance. Dune has three smaller concrete buildings around the exterior as well, which are the fire exits. The first is to the right and east after crossing the upper bridge, the second is to the right and south of the ship near a fence and the oasis, and the third is almost directly behind and to the west of the ship. Dune supports Rainy, Stormy, Foggy, Eclipsed, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, or Minefield weather by default. A waterfall can be seen to the left of the lower bridge during Rainy or Stormy weather. If players decided to overload and blow up ResearcherxB , debris from the ship can fall onto Dune's exterior in front of the ship on a hill. If players land on Dune in the future on that save file, a mild outbreak of white mold will be present on the exterior and two Infected Bunker Spiders will spawn on the exterior at the start of the day. plain.p-elder: The Elder is a hostile entity and variant of the Forest Keeper added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . It is a colossal humanoid figure with spikes jutting out of its body, skin resembling old tree bark, an open hole on its chest that is its mouth, and two eyes with a red layer around them. Similar to the Forest Keeper, the Elder will roam around until spotting players, raising its suspicion meter. The distance from the Elder , being uncrouched, moving, and sprinting all can increase the rate at which the Elder becomes suspicious. Once its suspicion meter has risen high enough for that specific player, it will begin chasing them until line of sight is broken for more than 3 seconds or the player dies. It will then search around the area it last saw the player for 9 seconds before beginning to roam around again. If the Elder grabs a player by coming into contact with them and successfully eats them, they will die and both their body and any items they were holding can not be recovered. If the Elder dies, its body will fall backwards and crush any player underneath it. The Elder exclusively spawns on Roart , having a 73.53% chance to spawn on the exterior during daytime. While the entry for the Elder is called "Forest Elder", players must type it as one word or type a minimum of "foreste" to not be redirected to the entry for the Forest Keeper. Forest Elder ⁠ FOREST ELDER Sigurd's danger level: 50% Scientific name: Satyrid-derceritas A very close relative to the Satyrid-proceritas. The Elders are a nearly extinct subspecies which are able to grow nearly twice as tall as the Forest Keepers due to their living conditions. However it is also because of their preferred environment that they never seek to leave the dense jungles which have become increasingly rarer. The Forest Elder shares a striking resemblance with its smaller counterpart. The main difference being a slightly whiter appearance and their eyes having a red protective layer against attacks from avian wildlife. It has been known that some tribes take the Elders as higher beings, believing they are men chosen by gods who have transformed to become the protectors of the woods they live in. Due to the striking similarity to the Forest keeper, read the data entry about the Forest keeper for more information on the Elder’s visual and physical evolution. plain.p-emma: Emma is a hostile entity and variant of the Ghost Girl added by Wesley's Ememy Variants . This entity is not to be confused with the other appearances of Emma during Forsaken weather or the unique trial found on the exterior of Roart . She is a young girl with a white dress, pale grey skin, long black hair, hollowed out eyes, and a noose around her neck. There is little to no difference between the Ghost Girl and Emma . She will appear behind her targeted player always accompanied by the sound of her hanging, muffling the player's audio if they look at her. After her targeted player has looked at her at least twice or ignored her at least three times, approaching, looking, or staring at her can cause her to begin chasing that player. She will decapitate and instantly kill that player on contact. There can be confusion on which Emma is the real entity versus the harmless and spooky jumpscares she does during Forsaken weather. However, players can always tell if she's the real entity depending on if she appears behind them, if their audio is muffled while looking at her, if only one player sees her at that time, and if this encounter happens later in the day. She can also still be cheesed by phasing into and crouching on top of the cupboard in the ship. Emma will spawn at exactly 02:00pm on a moon during Forsaken weather. This spawn does not contribute to total Power Level. While Emma does not have a bestiary or journal entry, this videotape does provide a little context on who she is. It is randomly available for purchase in the Gift Shop on Galetry and is only supposed to unlock Roart during Halloween season. Text ⁠ We are the hands that bury the deceased, you are the shovel that keep the hands from getting stained. We cannot allow the deceased to control who lives and who dies. Find the forsaken child, dispose of her body and we will let you out. Note that some of this audio may be difficult to hear in-game due to the muffling applied while looking at or being chased by Emma . Audio Action Sound Appearing Hanging Bell Chime Chasing Emma stalking a player at a distance. Emma chasing a player.
plain.p-empra: Home of the Emperor. Empra is happiness. Happiness is Empra . POPULATION: Killed. CONDITIONS: Hot, deserts, frequent sandstorms. FAUNA: A barren ecosystem. Home of the Emperor Unfinished Section This section seems unfinished. If you're a wiki editor, please help with completing this section. Empra is a dune with a dust storm with the city of Empra Empra can experience Rainy, Stormy, Earthquakes, Forsaken, Hallowed, or Hurricane weather by default. Empra has a default day speed multiplier of 0.5, meaning the player can stay on the moon for significantly longer. The Gilded Jester is an entity that exclusively can spawn in the interior of Empra . It is a variant of the Jester with a faster roaming speed, a significantly longer countdown before it begins cranking, and a significantly reduced cranking duration. Empra has a big cart with a lever that makes it go back and forth on the tracks. Scrap and items can travel back and forth on the cart. Inserting an apparatus into the center of the cart causes it to move faster . The following contains spoilers for completion. An apparatus must be inserted into the center of the cart. It is recommended to bring one beforehand due to how dangerous the interior of Empra can be. On the front end of the cart you can place the "Huge harold" (Atomic bomb) scrap that has at least one guaranteed spawn in the interior. Near the main entrance there is a mortar that needs to be interacted with to aim at the massive seed of assimilation in front of the main entrance. A lone fire exit can be found within the interior that leads to a control panel and this area is also accessible via jetpack. Interact with the control panel as prompted to fire the mortar and destroy the seed. This will anger the Overseer and cause him to unleash many tendrils around the exterior, and touching them will kill the player. Interact with the control panel again as prompted to move the cranes and lift up the tracks, which also pushes the cart back. Run to the cart and ride it back to the ship. Pull the cart lever again and you will be warned to jump off the cart immediately. The cart will then be rocketed into the Overseer and detonate the atomic bomb, killing him. After a cutscene, the destiny item "Chunk of harold" will spawn behind the ship. This allows the player to achieve Ending 2. Inserting the Empra videotape that has at least one guaranteed spawn as scrap within the interior of Hyx into the projector in Galetry . End: Acquire the destiny item "Chunk of harold" on the exterior after completing the moon exclusive content and insert it into the destiny item slot before taking off in the abandoned ship on Repress . Nothing quite remarkable today. 10:30 I woke up and per usual I brushed my teeth, did my hair, changed my clothes and went out for breakfast with the family in the grand hall. Had a laugh with my dad and went back home. 11:40 The cleaners knocked apparently, they should know to use the light by now. How many times would it take for them to remember I can’t hear the knocking. 13:30 We are back out to get lunch. I’ve been practicing art in the meantime. My parents are keen on letting me know it’s a worthless skill to have. They are no fun. 14:05 When we got home the neighbor passed by to update us on the state of the Emperor. He hasn’t been seen for weeks. Granted he’s not likely to leave his palace but he hasn’t been spotted in the windows either. 16:40 I’ve stayed home. There is not much out there to do. My parents went with the neighbor. 18:30 We had dinner in the grand hall. Apparently the Emperor’s absence is a common topic at the moment. I am starting to worry myself if I’m quite honest. 22:10 Watched a scary show with my parents. It’s difficult to understand what’s happening at times but that doesn’t make it less scary. They seemed to enjoy it at least. Diary entry 848. Strange occurrence on an otherwise regular day. 10:30 I woke up, brushed my teeth, did my hair and went with a slightly different style than usual, hoping someone would notice. I changed clothes and went out for breakfast with the family in the grand hall. 11:30 Yesterday I missed them so today I left the door open so I can see the cleaners arrive when they come and I won’t have to rely on my very functional hearing. 13:30 Lunch time, I’ve worked some more on my art while I waited for time to pass. 15:20 My parents came home for a bit and allowed me to have some sweets. Surprisingly they actually stayed with me until dinner time. 18:30 We went back to the grand hall for dinner. The emperor has not been seen yet. Maybe he’s resting. I’m sure it’s not easy to oversee an entire system. 22:10 That same show as yesterday came on so we watched it together. However in the middle it was interrupted by an emergency broadcast. There wasn’t any imagery nor any subtitles so I’ve no idea what was said. Whatever it was, it seemed to upset my parents, they looked concerned yet.. Relieved. It’s hard to describe. They quickly send me to bed. I’m sure they’ll tell me what that was tomorrow. Diary entry 849. This isn’t real. I am fairly certain this is a horrible nightmare. I will try to write what I saw. I’m fearful. 10:30 I woke up to a cold breeze. I walked over to brush my teeth, make up my hair and change clothes. I found it strange that I couldn’t feel my parents walk around, for a moment I assumed they were off to a neighbor again. Until I stepped out of my room. They were there, by the window, hanging from the ceiling. There was an empty noose next to them. I haven’t looked at them since. 12:00 I’ve been sobbing and crying. It’s not just my parents. I haven’t found a single living person. I think it’s everyone. I’ve looked out the window in the hallway. And I see more people hanging in the distance. I don’t believe this is real. 13:40 I went to an empty apartment on the top floor. I don’t have to see anyone here. I don’t want to see anyone else. 14:44 I felt the emergency bells ringing, it was a deep rumble to my skin which I’ve only felt during tests, I stepped out on the balcony to see what was going on, hoping there would be an answer but there he was. The Emperor. And at least a hundred noblemen all slowly marching out the palace. I screamed hoping for something to happen. Nothing. They kept walking. Nobody even bat an eye. I thought the Emperor would save us. Just like he had done with so many before us. I screamed and begged. It’s hard to write while I’m shaking. He stopped moving in the middle of the plaza. I thought he finally heard my screams but he kneeled and looked up. His mouth moved but it was too far for me to read what he said before he burst into this red mass. I couldn’t move. My body forced me to watch as he erupted into a swarm of tendrils reaching for the ground while he grew into something horrific. The noblemen kept walking and collapsed into him, vanishing into the mass. Last thing I saw before could take control and run was the red mass growing and pulsating. 16:12 I haven't quite calmed down but I’ve at least managed to calm my breathing. This doesn’t feel real. I don’t understand what is happening. Or if it even is. The Emperor would never let this happen. This would never happen. We’ve always been happy. I feel dizzy. There is a hole in my mind I cannot fill. It doesn’t make sense. Was it yesterday’s broadcast? What was even said? I wish I could fucking hear. It’s cold here. This must be a nightmare. It’s the only thing that makes sense. I know what they’re like, they’re just like this. They can be the worst reality while feeling completely real. This is the worst reality. My parents would never leave me like this, I know they wouldn’t. And the Emperor, it cannot be real. That must be it. I need to wake up. I have to wake up. I have to see mom and dad. This videotape can be found on Hyx only. Text ⁠ What is happiness? Is it your dirty workplace? Is it your filthy house? Is it your crippling need for a therapist because you realised the universe is completely stacked against you and you will likely suffer the same fate as millions of others as the pressure of your worthless life becomes to much for the imagination of the mind leading to eventual damnination? No! Happiness is the one who sends you money! Happiness is the one who created your job! Happiness is the one who protects you! Happiness is the Emperor! And if you work hard enough, You will be personally invited to live in his golden city! Happiness is Empra! Empra is happiness! Unfinished Section This section seems unfinished.
